推荐序一 · 专家特邀序

为历史留下记录

余秋雨 撰

去年秋天，我在瑞士的苏黎士湖畔有过一段时间的停留。这一带在今天的西方世界已经显得很不现代了，但我知道有关20世纪“现代人的最佳阐述却从这里发生，阐述者就是大名鼎鼎的荣格( Carl gustav jung）。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In the autumn of last year, I spent some time on the shores of Lake Zurich in Switzerland. To today's Western world, the region may seem rather unmodern, but it was here, I know, that the twentieth century's most compelling portrait of the modern man first emerged — painted by the famous Carl Gustav Jung.

荣格说，并不是一切生活在现代的人都可以称之为“现代人”。真正的现代人寥寥无几，他们既不站在昨天，也不站在明天，而是站在从昨天到明天的桥梁上。对这种过渡状态的充分感知，使他们同时领受到孤独，因为广大民众总是潜意识地被历史迷雾所笼罩，其中—部分还在倒退的本质外面戴上了伪现代的面具。只有真正的现代人知道自己是传统的产物，又是传统不忠的臣子，深知传统的缺失，日夜想以边缘性的创造去弥补，但心中又明白，今天的创造很快就会被超越，因此不能不时时陷于恐惧和烦恼。荣格希望人们能透过各种社会事件的表象，从心理和精神层面上去破译现代。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Jung wrote that not everyone who lives in the modern age can properly be called a modern man. True moderns are exceedingly rare. They stand neither on yesterday nor on tomorrow, but on the bridge connecting the two. A full awareness of this liminal state brings with it a certain loneliness, for the great mass of people remains unconsciously shrouded in the mists of history, some of them wearing masks of modernity over a fundamentally regressive core. Only the true modern man knows himself to be the product of tradition and, simultaneously, tradition's unfaithful servant — acutely aware of what tradition has left undone, driven day and night to make good those deficiencies through marginal acts of creation, yet knowing that today's creations will soon themselves be surpassed, leaving him perpetually haunted by fear and unease. Jung hoped that people could look past the surface of social events and decipher the modern world on psychological and spiritual levels.

也许出乎张忠谋先生意料之外，我在拜读他的自传时，不断想起荣格的上述论述。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Perhaps unexpectedly to Mr. Morris Chang, I found myself returning again and again to Jung's remarks as I read his autobiography.

张忠谋先生对大陆读者来说可能还有些陌生，但在台湾，则家喻户晓。以他为董事长的台湾积体电路公司无论从掌握的资金还是每年获利在台湾都名列前茅，他本人也在民意调查中成为最受尊敬的十大企业家之一。但奇异的是，十大企业家中只有他一人并非成长于台湾，而是五十四岁时才单枪匹马从美国回来。因此，他在台湾的骄人业绩，都创建于高龄岁月。他无疑是知识经济时代的杰出代表，却与人们心目中那些年轻的知识经济偶像那么不同，这不能不让人重新顺著荣格的思路，在更深刻的意义上来校正“现代人”的概念。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Mr. Chang may still be relatively unknown to readers on the mainland, but in Taiwan he is a household name. Under his chairmanship, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company ranks among the top in capital and annual profit. In polls of public opinion, he has been ranked among the ten most respected businessmen in the island. Yet curiously, he is the only one of those ten who did not grow up in Taiwan — returning alone from the United States at the age of fifty-four. All of his towering achievements were built in the later years of his life. He is unmistakably a standout figure of the knowledge economy, yet profoundly different from the young idols that figure occupies in people's imaginations. This compels one, following Jung's thread of thought, to recalibrate the very concept of the modern man at a deeper level.

现代人未必是年轻人。年轻人天然地习惯于现代，这是他们令人羡慕的优势，但并不是一切年轻人都能很好地发挥这种优势。有一些年轻人由于不知道历史发展的轨迹，反而常常站在陈旧的立场上向现代挑战，连当年中国的文革浩劫也是由一群年轻人以“破旧立新”的口号开始的，而实际上却是一个彻底颠倒新旧的悲剧。这种情形，在传统厚重而又争斗成性的族群中更容易发生。张忠谋先生的可贵，在于他以最隆重、最审慎的方式完成了一种文化转型，因此早早地就浑身松爽，成了一个现代创造者。

ReadShift 双语翻译

A modern man need not be young. The young are naturally accustomed to modernity — that is their enviable advantage — but not all young people can make good use of it. Some, lacking any sense of the trajectory of history, find themselves challenging modernity from a thoroughly outdated position. Even the Cultural Revolution in China was launched by a group of young people under the banner of "smashing the old and establishing the new," though in reality it proved to be a tragedy of utter inversion. Such patterns are more likely to occur among peoples with thick traditions and combative instincts. What distinguishes Mr. Chang is that he completed a cultural transformation in the most deliberate and careful manner, thereby freeing himself early and becoming a modern creator.

他的自传从一开始就写清楚了自己的两大文化背景。一是对民族救亡的激情，二是对中国文学的爱好。对民族救亡的激情应该说从他祖父一代就形成了，由“百日维新”，“民主”、“科学到颠沛流离，个人和家庭的命运与民族的安危紧紧相连，这就是他落笔第一句所说的“大时代”。“大时代”是他不可选择的背景，即使他一生器宇轩昂、忧国忧民，又为他设置了某种心理上的敏感和障碍。

另一个滋养他又束缚他的背景是中国文学，他从早年开始就接受了先秦诸子、《史记》、《三国演义》、《红楼梦》、桐城派和20世纪以来的中白话文学，甚至差一点要想去做中文作家，被长辈以难以谋生的理由阻止。这两大文化背景，各自都有美好的内涵，而且各自也都能通达现代，但是显而易见由这两大背景铸就的人，一定不是今天的张忠谋先生。张忠谋先生并没有遗弃它们，只让它们成为一种人生积淀而不是生命主干。

ReadShift 双语翻译

From the opening pages of his autobiography, he makes clear his two principal cultural backgrounds: a passionate devotion to national salvation and a deep love of Chinese literature. The fervor for national salvation dates, he suggests, to his grandfather's generation — from the Hundred Days' Reform, through the ideals of democracy and science, to the years of displacement, when the fate of individuals and families became inseparable from the survival of the nation. This is the "great era" he invokes in his very first sentence. The great era was a background he could not choose: it gave him a life of grand purpose and deep concern for his country and people, but it also planted a certain psychological sensitivity and obstacle within him.

ReadShift 双语翻译

The other background that both nourished and constrained him was Chinese literature — from his early years he absorbed the masters of the Pre-Qin period, the Records of the Grand Historian, the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, the Dream of the Red Chamber, the Tongcheng school, and the vernacular literature of the twentieth century. He nearly became a writer of fiction himself, only to be dissuaded by his elders on the grounds that it would not sustain a livelihood. Both of these cultural backgrounds carried rich meaning, and each could, in its own way, lead to modernity. But it is clear that a person forged from both of them would not have become the Morris Chang we know today. He did not abandon them; he simply allowed them to become sediment rather than the mainstay of his life.

这便是他在年轻时在美国完成的文化转型。

ReadShift 双语翻译

This was the cultural transformation he completed in America during his youth.

文化转型，要以文化的力量来完成。许多中国留学生熟悉了西方语言，习惯了西方生活，又掌握了专业技能，乍一看好像也完成了文化转型，其实未必，因为他们把持的只是“术”而不是“道”，而术在任何情况下都不能取代道与道之间的对峙和对话。好像冥冥中有一种力量在摆布，张忠谋先生的三叔高瞻远瞩地替他先选择了一年哈佛而不是立即进入最对应的麻省理工。他在哈佛的一年，几乎全方位地沉入了西方文明，从荷马、弥尔顿、莎士比亚、海明威、奥斯汀、萧伯纳，读到邱吉尔的二战回忆录和历届美国总统的演讲，同时订阅美国主要报刊、听音乐、看演剧、参观博物馆、参加球赛和舞会、结交美国朋友，如此覆盖辽阔又饥似渴，当然会影响专业学习的时间和精力，但从生命全程来看，真可以说是“磨刀不误砍柴工”，他从根本上对自己进行了一次重新塑造。张忠谋先生后来主持全世界最大的半导体产业，回台湾后又开创高科技企业，这种势头确实不是一般的中国留学生所能长久保持的，他的根本奥秘就在于那次从哈佛开始的重新塑造。他喜欢引用海明威的话，把自己在哈佛的获得说成是“可带走的盛宴”，并认为这餐盛宴滋补了他一生，包括他所从事的那些似乎与人文领域关系不大的科技工作，直到今天。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Cultural transformation must be accomplished through the power of culture. Many Chinese students abroad appeared, at first glance, to have undergone such a transformation: they mastered Western languages, grew accustomed to Western ways, and acquired professional skills. But that was not necessarily the case, for they possessed only technique, not the deeper principle — and technique, under any circumstances, cannot replace the Way, nor settle the confrontation and dialogue between one Way and another. As if some invisible hand were guiding events, Mr. Morris Chang's third uncle, with remarkable foresight, arranged for him to spend a year at Harvard rather than proceeding directly to MIT, the school more closely aligned with his technical ambitions. During that year at Harvard, he immersed himself comprehensively in Western civilization, reading Homer, Milton, Shakespeare, Hemingway, Austen, and Shaw, and moving on to Churchill's war memoirs and the speeches of American presidents.

ReadShift 双语翻译

He subscribed to the major American newspapers, listened to music, attended plays, visited museums, went to football games and dances, and made American friends. The range of his engagement was vast and his appetite fierce. It necessarily encroached on the time and energy he devoted to his technical studies, but in the larger arc of a life, it proved exactly what the Chinese saying warns against: sharpening the axe does not delay the chop.

ReadShift 双语翻译

Fundamentally, he remade himself. When he later presided over the world's largest semiconductor enterprise and went on to build high-technology companies in Taiwan, the force he brought to bear was something most Chinese students abroad could not sustain over the long term. The deeper reason lay in that act of self-remaking, which began at Harvard. He liked to quote Hemingway, describing what he gained there as "a moveable feast," and he believed that feast nourished him throughout his life — including the technological work he pursued, which seemed at first remove from the humanities — well into the present day.

我认为，张忠谋先生在自传里的这些叙述，举重若轻地说明了一个重大历史课题：一个揹负传统文化和救亡之梦的中国人也可以做出许多重要事情，但要在20世纪末仍然站在科技创新的最前沿而影响世界，一定要尽早地实行精神扩充和文化移位，使东西方文化在互相观照中彼此减压，特别是为过于沉重的中国文化减压，然后才能因无碍而保持最佳状态。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In my view, these passages from Mr. Chang's autobiography, handled with an effortless grace, illustrate a significant historical proposition: a Chinese person burdened with traditional culture and the dream of national salvation can accomplish much, but to stand at the cutting edge of technological innovation and influence the world as late as the twentieth century's close, one must undertake spiritual enlargement and cultural repositioning early on. Only by allowing Eastern and Western cultures to illuminate one another, and by easing the mutual pressure between them — particularly the pressure borne by an excessively weighty Chinese cultural tradition — can one remain unencumbered and operate at peak capacity.

在这里产生了一个很有意思的现象，张忠谋先生在自传中列举了早年阅读的诸多中国典籍，后来又列举了在美国大学读的诸多西方典籍，两类典籍加在一起不仅没有使笔端变得滞重，反而满篇轻盈。原来，当荷马遇到司马迁，当曹雪芹遇到莎士比亚，只会加添愉悦而不是愁苦。学问如夯土，种种不同质料的填埋只为筑造一个更便于活动的平台，而不是作仓库式的拥塞，稍稍搬放便没有了空间。

ReadShift 双语翻译

An intriguing phenomenon arises here. In his autobiography, Mr. Chang listed numerous classical Chinese works he had read in his early years and then enumerated many Western texts he encountered at American universities. The two bodies of reading together did not weigh down his prose; instead, the pages feel remarkably light. For when Homer meets Sima Qian, and Cao Xueqin meets Shakespeare, the result is only pleasure, never sorrow. Scholarship is like rammed earth: various materials of different composition are tamped down to build a platform that facilitates movement, not a warehouse of accumulation where space vanishes at the slightest rearrangement.

张忠谋先生虽然不是专治文史，但他由博返约，能进能出的态势深得治学玄机。任何一位现代创造者都需要为自己开拓一个空灵境界，而这个空灵又必须是丰厚积淀的结果。我们见到过很多无积淀的空灵，也见过很多不空灵的积淀，而很少见到像张忠谋先生这样，一方面被国际同行惊叹为“知识惊人，一方面又如荣格所说，站在边缘，面对荒原，深感无知。他如果像我们常见的那些学人，只被一学之僻、半书之专压得步履蹒跚，还会像今天这样处于创造前沿吗?文化，不管是中国文化还是西方文化，对很多人来说都是

ReadShift 双语翻译

Although Mr. Chang was not a specialist in the humanities, his ability to move from breadth back to essence — to enter and to exit with ease — revealed a profound wisdom of learning. Every modern creator must carve out for himself a spacious clarity, and that clarity must be the product of deep accumulation. We have seen much emptiness without substance and much substance without lightness, but seldom have we encountered someone like Mr. Chang, who, on one hand, left international colleagues astonished by the breadth of his knowledge, and on the other, like Jung described, stood at the edge confronting the wilderness, acutely aware of his own ignorance. Had he followed the path taken by too many scholars — crushed beneath a narrow specialization or a half-read canon — would he still be at the creative frontier today? Culture, whether Chinese or Western, has become for too many people a graveyard of creation.

好在经过生命的重新塑造，张忠谋先生具备了避开这些大大小小坟墓的自信和力量，他在1954年和1955年两次博士资格考试落第，承受了很大的打击，但只花了一个星期他就渡过了心理陷阱。他避开了一般中国留学生必然会走的路，即转校再读博士，然后终生从事教学研究，而是抬起头来自己去找工作。他在自传中有一段话说得很有味道。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Fortunately, having undergone this remaking, Mr. Chang acquired the confidence and strength to avoid these large and small graveyards. When he failed the doctoral qualifying exams at MIT in both 1954 and 1955, he suffered a serious blow, yet he moved past the psychological trap in a single week. He avoided the path that most Chinese students abroad would inevitably walk — transferring to another school to pursue a doctorate and spending a lifetime in teaching and research — and instead looked up and went in search of work himself. He wrote about this episode in his autobiography with considerable flavor.

许多年后，我把在麻省理工博土落第视为我一生的最大幸运，假如我通过考试，我一定会继续读博士，几年以后，也一定会读成，那以后做什么呢?最可能就是去工业界做研究工作，或留学校做教授，总之这会是一条学术研究之路。以我对工程的平平兴趣，我相信这条路不会走得太远。我也绝对不会进入半导体界，因那时半导体界根本不雇用机械博士。我也不会进入企业管理，因为这也不是博士常走的路。我的人生会完全两样，恐怕也不会在这里写自传了。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Many years later, I regarded failing the MIT doctoral qualifying exams as the greatest good fortune of my life. Had I passed, I would surely have continued toward the doctorate and completed it within a few years. And then what? Most likely I would have gone into industrial research or stayed at a university as a professor — in short, an academic track. Given my moderate interest in engineering, I'm convinced I would not have gone far on that road. I would certainly never have entered the semiconductor industry, since at that time no one in semiconductors hired mechanical engineering PhDs. Nor would I have moved into corporate management, which was never the common path for PhDs. My life would have been entirely different. I probably would not be writing this autobiography here.

一生最大的打击变成了一生最大的幸运，这里划分出了一种重大观念差异。张忠谋先生从这个事件进一步确立了不追慕虚名，不随波逐流的自主性、实效性理念。据我所知，三十年后他出任台湾工业技术研究院院长时大刀阔斧地整治那些永无成效的硏究计划，也正是这种实效性理念的延续。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The greatest blow of a lifetime becoming its greatest good fortune marks a profound difference in outlook. From this episode, Mr. Chang further solidified a commitment to autonomy and pragmatism — a refusal to chase hollow reputations or follow the crowd. To my knowledge, thirty years later when he assumed the presidency of the Industrial Technology Research Institute in Taiwan and ruthlessly dismantled research programs that had produced nothing of substance, he was extending the same pragmatic philosophy.

在现代高科技企业中追求实际成效，当然与创新有关，因此实效理念后面紧跟著的必然是创新理念。没有创新立即就会被淘汰，根本无成效可言。这部自传中有一段描写张忠谋先生普热情效力的希凡尼亚公司。由于主管半导体部的领导阶层故步自封，终于衰败，张忠谋先生去视察待售仪器设备的场景，很有感染力。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The pursuit of practical results in modern high-tech enterprises is, of course, connected to innovation, and it follows naturally that the philosophy of results is followed by a philosophy of innovation. Without innovation, one is eliminated immediately and results become impossible. The autobiography contains a passage describing Morris Chang's devotion to Sylvania, the company where he spent years. Under leaders of its semiconductor division who grew complacent and insular, the business declined, and Chang's account of inspecting the equipment slated for sale is vivid and moving.

我走进庞大而空洞的厂房，举目望见的是有裂痕的墙壁，陈旧的桌椅，过时的设备。每说一句话，就听到在静寂中漂荡的回音。整个气氛使我感到无比的凄凉。我走到从前办公室的地方，隔间早巳被重隔好几次。重循当年常从办公室割实验室的脚步，当年四周是年轻人的笑声，现在只有如死亡般的寂静。我站在厨房中间，静默了许久。陪我的人似乎知道我的思念，久不出一言。

ReadShift 双语翻译

I walked through the vast, hollow plant. The walls were cracked; the desks and chairs were old; the equipment was out of date. Every word I spoke echoed in the silence. The whole atmosphere struck me as unbearably desolate. I came to the place where my former office had been; the cubicles had been partitioned into smaller rooms many times over. Retracing the steps I once took from the office to the laboratory, where years ago there had been laughter and young voices, I found only a silence like death. I stood in the middle of the kitchen and was quiet for a long time. The person with me seemed to know what I was thinking and said nothing.

饱受战争的惊吓The Shock of War

这从小就养成的阅读习惯，一生都保持着。我刚10岁那年，日本偷袭珍珠港，第二次世界大战自此爆发。我对童年的记忆，珍珠港事件可说是一个分水岭。珍珠港事件以前的记忆比较模糊，以后则很清晰。日本在偷袭珍珠港后数小时，立即开始攻击香港。我家那时住在九龙，1941年12月8日清晨听到炸弹声。

ReadShift 双语翻译

This reading habit, formed in childhood, stayed with me all my life. When I was ten, Japan attacked Pearl Harbor, and the Second World War erupted. Of my childhood memories, Pearl Harbor stands as a watershed: what came before is blurred, what came after is vivid. Within hours of striking Pearl Harbor, the Japanese launched their assault on Hong Kong. We were living in Kowloon then, and on the morning of December 8, 1941, we heard the bombs.

语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

文中用“分水岭”来形容珍珠港事件。把抽象的历史节点比喻为地理上的分水岭，使其变得具体可感，突出前后两个人生阶段的截然不同。The text uses “watershed” to describe Pearl Harbor—rendering an abstract historical moment as a geographical divide, making it tangible and emphasizing the stark contrast between two phases of a life.

“以前的记忆比较模糊，以后则很清晰”形成鲜明对照。模糊与清晰之间，衬托出战争带来的强烈冲击，也让文本节奏有了一种张力。The juxtaposition of “before, memories were hazy; after, they were vivid” creates a sharp contrast. The interplay between indistinctness and clarity underscores the violent impact of war—and lends the prose a taut, tensile rhythm.

第一段由“体质不好”引出母亲“让吃鱼肝油、炖鸡汤”；由“没有兄弟姐妹、不常打球”引出“常独自在家”；再由“独处”引向“读书”，最后自然推出“养成终身习惯”。层层递进，逻辑流畅。The opening passage proceeds through a chain of linked causes: frail health leads to cod-liver oil and chicken soup; having no siblings and rarely playing ball leads to time alone at home; solitude leads to reading; and reading naturally yields a lifelong habit. Each link builds on the last with seamless, cumulative logic.

“清晨听到炸弹声”没有渲染血腥，仅用一个听觉细节，就让战争的骤然降临跃然纸上，余味悠长。“Hearing the bombs in the early morning” avoids any graphic depiction of bloodshed. With a single auditory detail, the sudden descent of war is rendered with startling immediacy—and a lingering aftertaste.

那天早上天有考试，所以还是步行上学。到了学校，才开始了解情形，知道日本人已在打九龙。当然考试也取消了，课也没有了，赶快回家。我家住在比较冷清的区域，父亲以为迁到旅馆里会比较安全，当天我们全家三人带了一个女佣就搬到九龙酒店(在今日半岛酒店的后面)。3天后，九龙被日军占领，以后香港又守了十几天，但在圣诞夜(12月24日)英军投降。自日军于12日开始攻击到年底，我们都躲在九龙酒店。

ReadShift 双语翻译

There had been an examination scheduled that morning, so I walked to school as usual. Only upon arriving did I learn the truth: the Japanese were already attacking Kowloon. The exam was cancelled, classes were suspended, and I hurried home. We lived in a comparatively quiet district, and my father thought it safer to move to a hotel. That very day, the three of us, along with a maidservant, checked into the Kowloon Hotel (behind what is now the Peninsula Hotel). Three days later, the Japanese occupied Kowloon; Hong Kong Island held out for a little over two weeks, until the British surrendered on Christmas Eve (December 24). From the Japanese attack on the twelfth to the end of the year, we hid in the Kowloon Hotel.

幸而大家都很安全，却也受到一些惊吓。起先是炸弹声，后来常听见街上的枪声，更常听见日军隔海攻击香港的炮声。这几个星期几乎全部都在戒严状态下，我们不能、也不想出旅馆。旅馆里的食物渐渐吃尽，后来吃的都是罐头食物，到最后罐头也几乎吃尽，幸而那时已开始解严了。解严后，父母亲回到家，发现房子并没有被战火损毁，但是在英军已撤出、日军尚未驻入九龙期间，家中已被歹徒抢劫，寄居在我家的亲戚和留家的女佣都饱受惊吓。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Fortunately, we were all safe, though not without some fright. At first came the bombs, then the frequent crackle of gunfire in the streets, and more often still the thunder of Japanese artillery shelling Hong Kong Island across the harbour. For nearly all of those weeks the city was under martial law; we could not leave the hotel, and did not want to. The hotel's food gradually ran out, and we lived on canned provisions until those, too, were nearly gone—luckily, the curfew had begun to lift by then. When my parents finally returned home, they found the house undamaged by the war, but looted by thieves during the interval when the British had withdrawn and the Japanese had not yet entered Kowloon. The relatives staying with us and the maidservant who had remained behind were deeply shaken.

10岁在香港。At age ten, in Hong Kong.

我们在日据的香港又住了一年，在这一年中，香港的市面渐渐恢复，我小学毕业，父亲也仍在同一银行做事。日本人占领的迹象到处皆是，市内重要地点都有所谓"皇军"站岗，经过的路人都要对他们鞠躬。我就读的小学里忽然多了好几位亲日的教师，一有机会就对我们讲英美兵如何只知道喝酒享受，一听见枪声就立刻向后逃。父亲在新政权管制下工作，更有难言的感受。

We spent another year in occupied Hong Kong. During that year the city's commercial life gradually revived; I graduated from elementary school, and my father remained at the same bank. Signs of the occupation were everywhere: at every important spot in the city, so-called "Imperial soldiers" stood guard, and passersby were required to bow to them. Several pro-Japanese teachers suddenly appeared at my school; at every opportunity they told us how the British and American soldiers knew only how to drink and enjoy themselves, and how at the first sound of gunfire they fled. My father worked under the rule of the new regime, and bore humiliations he could not speak of.

所以在1942年底，父亲决定举家迁往重庆。重庆是那时中国的临时首都，号称"陪都"。父亲又决定在去重庆前，先到上海、宁波省视我的祖父母及外祖父母。

So at the end of 1942, my father decided to move the whole family to Chongqing. Chongqing was then China's provisional capital, known as the "wartime capital." Before departing, my father resolved to visit my grandparents, both paternal and maternal, in Shanghai and Ningbo.

语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

这段文字运用了艾萨克森风格中典型的「日常细节承载历史重量」手法：从一场普通的考试写起，以极其克制的笔调记录战争临近时的个人感知。逻辑层面上呈现清晰的因果链——「有考试→步行上学→到校知详情→考试取消→赶回家→父亲决策搬迁」，每一步都环环相扣，没有赘述，却让读者感受到时间的紧迫与局势的急速恶化。This passage exemplifies the Isaacson-esque technique of letting ordinary details carry the weight of history. It opens with a routine examination, and records, in a deliberately restrained tone, the shifting perceptions of an individual as war approaches. Beneath the surface, the narrative forms an unmistakable causal chain—exam scheduled, walk to school, news arrives, exam cancelled, rush home, father decides to move—each link connecting without a wasted word, yet conveying the mounting urgency and the swift deterioration of events.

最精妙之处在于省略主语的叙事策略：前半段以「天有考试」开启，主角的存在感隐藏在动作背后，直到「才知道日本人已在打九龙」，历史的巨浪才真正扑面而来。父亲的最后决策「以为迁到旅馆里会比较安全」一语，既是个人求生本能，也是战时香港平民命运的缩影。The most exquisite touch lies in the narrative strategy of omitting the subject. The first half opens with “there was an exam that day,” the protagonist’s presence hidden behind the actions, until the moment “only then did we learn that the Japanese were already attacking Kowloon”—when the great wave of history truly rushes in. The father’s final decision, “thinking it would be safer to move into a hotel,” is at once an instinct for survival and a miniature portrait of Hong Kong civilians trapped in the tides of war.

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text
**九龙战役（Battle of Kowloon，1941年12月8日–12月12日）**
是香港保卫战的第一阶段。日军于1941年12月8日凌晨入侵香港，同日珍珠港事件爆发。驻港英军及加拿大联军在九龙地区进行顽强抵抗，但终因火力悬殊，于12月12日撤守维多利亚港南岸。12月25日，香港总督杨慕琦投降，香港进入日军占领时期（1941–1945）。 **The Battle of Kowloon (December 8–12, 1941)**
was the first phase of the Battle of Hong Kong. Japanese forces invaded Hong Kong in the early hours of December 8, 1941—the very day of the attack on Pearl Harbor. British and Canadian troops defending the Kowloon peninsula mounted a determined resistance, but were ultimately overwhelmed by superior firepower and withdrew to the southern shore of Victoria Harbour on December 12. On December 25, Governor Sir Mark Young surrendered, and Hong Kong entered a period of Japanese occupation (1941–1945).
**艾萨克森传记风格要点**
- 以具体细节（考试、步行）切入宏大历史
- 避免情绪渲染，用事实本身传递张力
- 人物动机简洁交代，不过度心理描写
- 时间线清晰，因果关系明确 **Key Elements of Isaacson's Biographical Style**
- Opens grand historical narratives with concrete details (an exam, a walk)
- Avoids emotional embellishment, letting facts convey the tension
- States character motivations succinctly, without excessive psychological probing
- Maintains a clear timeline and explicit causal relationships

我们在1942年底乘船到上海，停留了大约3个月的时间，在过旧历年时，回故乡宁波住了几星期。对11岁的我，在上海的3个月是很兴奋的时光，我见到了多年不见、记忆中已模糊的亲戚，又第一次经历到当时中国最繁华的都市。这3个月内，父亲也积极准备我们去重庆的旅程。那时虽已有许多亲友从沦陷区到自由区，但要越过前线，毕竟有不少风险，而且旅程要经过许多交通不便的地方。在战时物资缺乏，一切不便的环境下，这趟旅程不能不说是父亲相当冒险、但又抱着满怀重返祖国热情的尝试。父母亲那时才三十几岁，正是最敢冒险的年龄。

ReadShift 双语翻译

By late 1942, we had sailed to Shanghai and remained there for roughly three months, returning to our hometown of Ningbo for a few weeks during the Lunar New Year. For an eleven-year-old, those months in Shanghai were electric. I reconnected with relatives whose faces had long faded from memory, and I experienced firsthand the most thriving metropolis in wartime China. During that same window, my father began quietly organizing our departure for Chongqing. While numerous relatives had already relocated from the occupied coastal zones to the nationalist-held interior, crossing the frontline still carried substantial peril, and the route traversed regions with virtually no modern infrastructure. Amid wartime scarcity and compounded hardship, the journey amounted to something of a daring experiment by my father—one fueled not merely by survival, but by a fervent desire to return to the heart of the nation. My parents were both in their early thirties, an age that naturally favors risk over caution.

冒死横穿战线Braving the Frontline

1943年3月下旬，我们自上海出发。出发时只知道大概的途径，至于整个旅程要多久，用什么交通工具，路上住什么地方，都只有父亲打听来的不完全、不确定的情报。旅程的第一段是最可靠的一段，就是坐火车到南京，再转火车到徐州。徐州那时在日军手里，但已接近国军与日军交战的前线。通过徐州后的目标是洛阳，洛阳在国军手里，所以自徐州到洛阳，要穿过战线。从徐州到洛阳，我们用尽各种不同交通工具，能搭卡车时搭卡车，有黄包车或三轮车时搭黄包车或三轮车，没有任何车辆时就走路。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In late March 1943, we set out from Shanghai. At the start we knew only the general route; how long the journey would take, what transport we would use, and where we would sleep were questions answered only by the fragmentary and uncertain information my father had gathered. The first leg was the most dependable: a train to Nanjing, then a connecting train to Xuzhou. Xuzhou was then in Japanese hands, but close to the front where Nationalist and Japanese forces were fighting. Beyond Xuzhou, our target was Luoyang, which the Nationalists held—so between the two cities we had to cross the battle line. We used every kind of conveyance imaginable: trucks when trucks were available, rickshaws or pedicabs when there were rickshaws or pedicabs, and our own two feet when there was nothing at all.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Sketchy at best—信息支离破碎、不可靠，仅凭零散线索作出的粗略判断。
Piece together—把零散的信息片段整合成完整图景。
Fragmented intelligence—不连续、不成体系的零散情报或信息。
Deploy every available means—想尽办法、调动所有手段达成目标。
Compounded hardship—多重困难叠加造成的恶劣处境。
Fervent desire—满腔热情、难以抑制的迫切愿望。
Daring experiment—高风险、结果难料的冒险之举。
A phase that naturally favors risk over caution—指敢闯敢试、以机会为先的人生或企业阶段。
语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

三个并列分句层层推进，以节奏感强烈的排比结构再现旅途的曲折与父亲的机变，读来如画面切换，生动紧凑。Three parallel clauses advance in steady escalation, their rhythmic cadence recreating both the rugged journey and the father’s resourcefulness—each image flickering past like a scene cut, vivid and taut.

"sketchy at best"（极度不确定）与"the most dependable"（最可靠）形成鲜明对照，凸显即便最稳妥的第一程也建立在脆弱信息之上，强化了战时出行的艰险氛围。“Sketchy at best” and “the most dependable” stand in stark opposition, underscoring that even the surest first leg rests on fragile intelligence—heightening the perilous atmosphere of wartime travel.

以"quietly organizing"收束父亲行动的低调与隐忍，与后文"daring experiment"的大胆形成内在张力，人物性格不言自明。“Quietly organizing” captures the father’s low-key forbearance, while its quiet restraint plays against the boldness of the later “daring experiment”—the man’s character revealed without a word of direct commentary.

外链知识窗 · Beyond the Text
战时重庆：1937–1946年中华民国战时陪都，大量政府机构、高校与民众内迁至此，成为抗战大后方政治、经济与文化中心。 Wartime Chongqing: From 1937 to 1946, Chongqing served as the provisional wartime capital of the Republic of China. A vast number of government agencies, universities, and civilians were relocated there, making it the political, economic, and cultural center of the rear area during the War of Resistance.
徐州—洛阳走廊：1944年豫湘桂战役前，徐州（日军控制）至洛阳（国军控制）之间为敌我交界地带，是战时从华东通往西南的重要陆路通道，路况极差，需多种交通工具接力。 The Xuzhou–Luoyang Corridor: Before the Battle of Henan–Hunan–Guangxi in 1944, the area between Xuzhou (under Japanese control) and Luoyang (held by Nationalist forces) formed the front line between enemy and friendly territory. It was a vital overland route linking East China to the Southwest during the war, but the roads were in extremely poor condition and required a relay of multiple modes of transport.
自由区与沦陷区：抗战时期，中国政府控制的“自由区”（以重庆为中心）与日军占领的“沦陷区”之间的人员流动受到严格限制，穿越前线往往需依靠秘密通道或非官方路线。 Free Zone and Occupied Zone: During the War of Resistance, movement of people between the government-controlled “Free Zone” (centered on Chongqing) and the Japanese-occupied areas was strictly restricted. Crossing the front lines often required relying on secret passages or unofficial routes.

穿越前线时，我们当然选择一段无战事的前线，但也绝不担保一定不会有枪炮，那一段是完全走路的。从徐州到洛阳的旅程花了好几天，每晚或在小旅店，或在小店，或在庙宇投宿。战时在接近前线的地方，常有军队来检查旅客。记得有一天晚上，来检查我们的居然是中国军队，父母亲的笑容在离开上海后，第一次显露出来了！洛阳是古都，也是我们到自由区的第一个大城市。我们在这里休息了几天，也顺便去寻访古迹。从洛阳到西安有火车，但这一段还需冒一个险。

ReadShift 双语翻译

When crossing the frontline, we naturally chose a stretch where no fighting was in progress, though there was never any guarantee it would remain quiet; that entire segment we covered on foot. The journey from Xuzhou to Luoyang took several days, and each night we lodged wherever we could—a small inn, a little shop, or a temple. In wartime, near the front, soldiers frequently stopped travelers for inspection. I remember one evening when the troops who came to check us turned out, unexpectedly, to be Chinese. It was the first time my parents had smiled since leaving Shanghai! Luoyang was an ancient capital and the first major city we reached in the free zone. We rested there for a few days and took the opportunity to visit its historic sites. There was a railway from Luoyang to Xi'an, but that leg still required braving a risk.

因为火车经潼关时，日军的炮位正在黄河的对岸，听说每月总有好几次要对火车射击，所以铁路局派在这段行走的火车，都是最旧的火车，即使被击毁，损失也不致太大。这一段路程号称"闯关车"(闯潼关)，都在晚上行驶。记得我们乘"闯关车"那晚，到了危险地段，火车速度突然增快，车厢全黑，虽挤满了人，但大家都屏住气，突然无声，耳中只听到火车疯狂前进的咔嗒嗒、咔嗒嗒声。过了一会，火车缓慢下来，车厢灯光复明，大家知道危险期已过，兴奋地欢呼起来。从洛阳到西安要经过关中平原，少年最深的印象是：在户外停留不久，脸上、衣服上就是一层黄沙。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Because the railway passed through Tongguan, where the Japanese artillery was positioned across the Yellow River and was said to fire on trains several times each month, the railway bureau assigned its oldest trains to this stretch—even if one were destroyed, the loss would not be great. This service was known as the "Tongguan run" (running the gauntlet of Tongguan), and it travelled only at night. I remember the night we rode it: at the danger zone the train suddenly accelerated, the carriages went dark, and though they were packed with people, everyone held their breath in absolute silence, the only sound the frantic clackety-clack of the wheels racing forward. After a while the train slowed, the lights came back on, and everyone knew the danger was past, bursting into excited cheers. From Luoyang to Xi'an we crossed the Guanzhong Plain, and my deepest impression as a boy was this: stay outdoors briefly and your face and clothes would be coated with a layer of yellow dust.

关中平原是许多朝代的发迹地，也是古代兵马驰骋之地。那时我已读了一点历史，从火车窗口眺望，常有怀古之情。在西安，我们住在西京招待所，这是离开上海后，第一个比较舒适的旅舍。西安有不少名胜古迹，我们也去了附近的华清池，重寻千年前唐明皇和杨贵妃的遗迹。那时大家对"西安事变"记忆犹新，我们也去访寻事变的遗迹。在西安又住了好几天。西行至此，下一个目的地是成都。从西安到成都没有铁路，只能乘大卡车。那时的大卡车理论上只运货，不载客，但司机常"捉黄鱼"，也就是偷运客人，收费为外快。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The Guanzhong Plain was where many dynasties had risen, and where the armies of antiquity had ridden. By then I had read a little history, and gazing from the train window I often felt the stirrings of nostalgia for the past. In Xi'an we stayed at the Xijing Guesthouse—the first genuinely comfortable lodging since leaving Shanghai. The city abounded in famous sites; we visited the nearby Huaqing Pool, retracing the traces of Emperor Xuanzong and his consort Yang Guifei a thousand years earlier. The "Xi'an Incident" was still fresh in everyone's memory, and we went to see its sites as well. We lingered several more days in Xi'an. Our next destination was Chengdu, and since there was no railway from Xi'an to Chengdu, we had to travel by heavy truck. In those days the trucks were theoretically for freight only, but drivers commonly "caught yellow fish"—that is, smuggled passengers aboard, pocketing the fares as side income.

乘客坐在露天货物上面，非但颠簸得很厉害，而且如果不用力拉住绑货的绳子，还有被颠出车外的危险。西安到成都的公路狭窄而且险陡，当时我深深地领会到"蜀道难，难于上青天"的道理，但是沿途山景极为雄壮。成都是古蜀国之都，对喜欢《三国演义》的我，当然又是一个喜悦的经验。从成都到重庆，我们坐公共汽车，那时已近最后目的地，我们都非常兴奋。自上海到重庆，一共走了五十几天，这是一次很辛苦的旅程，没有好的交通工具，除了几个大城市外，也没有好的住的地方。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Passengers sat on the open cargo, and the ride was not only brutally bumpy—unless you clung hard to the ropes binding the freight, you risked being thrown right off the truck. The road from Xi'an to Chengdu was narrow and perilously steep; riding it, I understood deeply why it was said that "the road to Shu is harder than climbing to heaven." Yet the mountain scenery along the way was magnificent. Chengdu was the capital of the ancient Shu kingdom, and for a boy who loved *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*, it was another delight. From Chengdu we continued to Chongqing by bus; nearing our final destination, we were all in high spirits. From Shanghai to Chongqing the whole trek had taken over fifty days—a grueling journey with poor transport and, apart from the big cities, no decent places to stay.

写到此处，我忍不住将那次旅行与今天的旅行作一比较。如今的每一次出行，行程安排得严丝合缝，交通工具和住宿都经过精心挑选，一切追求极致的舒适与享受。而当年的旅途，则完全是另一番景象。两者之间，犹如天地之别。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Writing this now, I can't help but set that journey against the way we travel today. Every modern trip is meticulously planned—transportation, accommodations, everything accounted for in advance, all engineered for maximum comfort. Compared with what we endured, it's like comparing two entirely different worlds.

在过去的几十年里，我早已行路百万。但无论后来的人生中有多少舒适甚至奢华的旅行，令我魂牵梦萦的、对我最有意义的、在我脑海中留下最深印记的旅程，始终是十一岁那年从上海跋涉到重庆的那一段。

Once we arrived in Chongqing, the problem of schooling became my greatest trial—and my parents' deepest worry. I had spent only half a semester in junior high in Hong Kong before the war consumed those months, and now I faced the prospect of entering directly into the eighth grade. The best school in town, widely considered, was Nankai Middle School on Shapingba Hill. Each year it held entrance examinations, but the slots were few and the applicants countless. There was another route—the summer school program that Nankai ran each year. Exceptional performance could earn a direct placement, but even that path was far from easy.

记得刚到重庆不久，母亲与一位显要的夫人打牌，谈起了我的入学问题。母亲说我想考南开，那位夫人十分直率地回答："考不进去的，还是快一点找关系、讲人情吧。"那时我也在场，听到这句话，心里顿时凉了半截，因为我深知父母没有什么门路可托。

I remember clearly: soon after we arrived, my mother was playing cards with the wife of a prominent official when the subject of my schooling came up. My mother mentioned that I hoped to enter Nankai. The woman, remarkably forthright, replied simply: "He won't get in. You'd do better to find connections." I happened to be nearby, and I felt my heart sink. I knew then, as I know now, that our family had no such connections to draw upon.

母亲最终决定让我参加南开的暑期班——既可温习功课，又争取成绩优异而被保送的可能。南开有一项规定：所有学生必须住校。这首先是出于现实的考虑：沙坪坝距重庆市区不过二三十公里，但当时的交通条件极差，走读对绝大多数学生而言根本不可能。然而，抛开现实的因素不谈，强制住校实际上是一项极好的教育政策。在我整个求学经历中，学得最快、心情最愉快、也结交了最多挚友的岁月，恰恰都是住在学校宿舍的那些日子。

My mother ultimately decided that I should attend Nankai's summer program, which would allow me to review my studies and, hopefully, earn a place through outstanding performance. Nankai required all students to live on campus, a rule driven initially by practical necessity—Shapingba was only twenty or thirty kilometers from central Chongqing, but the roads were so poor that commuting was impossible for most families. Beyond that practical consideration, however, I came to believe that boarding was one of the best educational decisions I ever experienced. Looking back across the arc of my schooling, the periods in which I learned most quickly, felt most at ease, and formed the closest friendships were always those spent in the dormitory.

语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

首段以"现代旅行 vs. 战时跋涉"建立强烈的时空反差，不是简单铺陈细节，而是让读者感受到两种人生经验之间的断裂——"two entirely different worlds"这一表述，既克制又极具穿透力。The opening paragraph develops a stark temporal contrast between modern travel and wartime journey—not through mere exposition, but by making the reader feel the rupture between two entirely different worlds. The phrase "two entirely different worlds" is both restrained and piercing.

对话直接引用显要夫人的原话，不加评论，让事实本身产生冲击力。"I felt my heart sink"用身体感受替代心理描述，是传记写作中"show, don't tell"的典型手法。By quoting the eminent lady directly and offering no commentary, the narrative lets the raw fact land with force. The line "I felt my heart sink" substitutes a physical sensation for psychological description—a classic instance of "show, don't tell" in biographical writing.

结尾处"Looking back across the arc of my schooling"以成熟的成年视角回望童年，将个人经历嵌入更长的生命轨迹，赋予日常抉择以命运的重量——这是艾萨克森传记最核心的叙事特征：在平凡的选择中，照见一个人未来的轮廓。The closing phrase, "Looking back across the arc of my schooling," turns a mature adult gaze upon childhood, embedding personal experience within a longer arc of life and granting ordinary decisions the weight of destiny. This is the signature narrative device of Isaacson's biographies: in everyday choices, we glimpse the outline of a future self.

"现代旅行 vs. 战时跋涉"构成全篇的情感底色，作者用"like comparing two entirely different worlds"将两种极端经验并置，让读者直接感知两种人生经验之间的断裂，为后文的记忆深度埋下伏笔。"Modern travel versus wartime trek" sets the emotional undertone of the entire piece. By placing these two extreme experiences side by side through the phrase "like comparing two entirely different worlds," the author lets readers feel the rupture directly, planting the seed for the memoir's depth to come.

显要夫人的直白回应"你靠关系吧"与"我们没有任何关系可以动用"形成强烈反差。作者没有用任何评论性语言，仅以"I felt my heart sink"一笔带过——这是典型的"show, don't tell"手法，让事实自身产生冲击力。The eminent lady's blunt reply—"You'll have to use connections"—stands in sharp contrast to "we have no connections to pull." Without a single word of commentary, the author passes over it with just "I felt my heart sink," a model of "show, don't tell" that lets the facts strike with their own force.

南开强制住校的规则，表面上是"driven by practical necessity"（交通不便），但在回望的视角下被重新诠释为"one of the best educational decisions"——这段反思揭示了传记写作最核心的叙事策略：**用成年后的成熟视角回望童年选择，赋予日常决定以命运的重量**。The school's mandatory-residency rule at Nankai, ostensibly "driven by practical necessity" (the inconvenient commuting distances), is reinterpreted in retrospect as "one of the best educational decisions." This reflection reveals the central narrative strategy of biography: using a mature adult perspective to look back on childhood choices, giving ordinary decisions the weight of destiny.

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text
**南开中学与战时教育迁徙**：抗日战争期间，大批教育机构内迁至重庆。南开中学作为北方名校的代表，其辗转南迁本身即是中国近代教育史的一段缩影。沙坪坝一带因此形成了战时著名的"文化区"，汇聚了多所重要中学。 **Nankai Middle School and the Wartime Migration of Education**: During the War of Resistance against Japan, a large number of educational institutions were relocated inland to Chongqing. As a representative of prestigious northern schools, Nankai Middle School’s arduous journey southward was itself a microcosm of the history of modern Chinese education. The Shapingba area thus became a renowned wartime "cultural district," gathering many important secondary schools.
**暑期班制度（Summer Bridge Program）**：在教育资源竞争激烈的体系中，暑期衔接班既是学术补救机制，也是精英选拔的隐性通道。这种模式至今仍在众多顶尖教育机构中保留，其核心逻辑是通过高强度短期训练筛选出具备坚韧品质与学习潜力的学生。 **The Summer Bridge Program**: In a system marked by intense competition for educational resources, the summer bridge program functions both as a mechanism for academic remediation and as a hidden channel for elite selection. This model persists in many top-tier educational institutions to this day, its core logic being the use of intensive short-term training to identify students with resilience and intellectual promise.
**"大时代"的历史修辞**：中文语境中的"大时代"并非单纯的时间标记，而是一种价值判断——它暗示个体命运与历史洪流深度交织，个人的挣扎与抉择具有超越自身时代的意义。艾萨克森在写作《爱因斯坦传》时，同样将科学家的个人轨迹嵌入了两次世界大战的历史背景中。 **The Historical Rhetoric of the "Great Era"**: In the Chinese context, the term "great era" is not a mere temporal marker but a value judgment—one that implies a profound interweaving of individual destiny with the currents of history, wherein personal struggles and choices carry significance beyond their own time. In writing Einstein: His Life and Universe, Walter Isaacson similarly embeds the scientist’s personal trajectory within the historical backdrop of the two World Wars.

重庆全家福。后排右四为父亲，右五是我，母亲坐在前排中间，那时我13岁，就读南开中学，剃光头。A family photograph in Chongqing. In the back row, my father is fourth from the right and I am fifth from the right; my mother sits in the center of the front row. I was thirteen, attending Nankai Middle School, with a shaved head.

当然，战时重庆的学生住宿生活相当艰苦，南开已经比别的学校好，但与现在的学生住宿生活相比，真如两个世界。宿舍是一个大统间，有一条长的走廊，走廊左右是无数双层的床铺，每四张床（即八个床铺）形成一个小间，小间与走廊无隔离，小间与小间之间也只有短墙相隔。宿舍里只有床，没有别的家具，读书必须去教室，衣服放在箱子里，箱子则塞在床下面。宿舍里臭虫猖獗，干净的铺盖搬入宿舍几天后，就开始有臭虫。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Of course, life for wartime students in Chongqing was hard—Nankai was better than most schools, but compared with student boarding today it was like a different world. The dormitory was one vast hall with a long corridor down the middle; on either side stretched row upon row of double-decker bunks. Every four beds—eight berths—formed a cubicle, open to the corridor and separated from the next cubicle only by a low partition wall. The dorm held nothing but beds. For study we went to the classrooms; clothes went into trunks, and the trunks went under the beds. Bedbugs infested the place—clean bedding carried into the dorm would be crawling with them within days.

刚被臭虫咬时，常整夜睡不好，但久而久之倒也开始习惯，尽管第二天早上总有几处红斑，但晚上照样酣睡。每几个月，学校会找一天杀虫，大家都把床架搬到蒸汽房去蒸，但杀虫的效果只能延续几天，几天后臭虫又出现了。住在南开中学时，每天三顿伙食都定时在饭堂用。战时内地一般食用的米都是很粗糙、黄颜色的米，吃惯了倒也不觉得怎样。饭菜以素食为主，但每星期有一餐「牙祭」，桌上有一道例如红烧肉类的奢侈荤菜，平常的饭菜可以说与鱼肉绝缘。榨菜是四川的特产，我们几乎每餐都有榨菜。有时菜吃完了而肚子尚未饱，就用酱油拌饭继续吃。

ReadShift 双语翻译

At first the bites kept me awake through whole nights, but in time I grew used to them; though there were always a few red welts the next morning, I slept soundly anyway. Every few months the school would devote a day to extermination: everyone carried the bed frames to the steam room to be fumigated. The effect lasted only a few days before the bedbugs returned. At Nankai all three meals were served at fixed hours in the dining hall. In wartime the interior generally ate coarse, yellowish rice—once accustomed to it, we didn't mind. Meals were mostly vegetarian, but once a week came the "ya ji," when a luxurious meat dish such as braised pork appeared on the table; on ordinary days fish and meat were unheard of. Pickled mustard tuber was a Sichuan specialty, and we had it at nearly every meal. Sometimes, when the food ran out before our hunger did, we poured soy sauce over rice and kept eating.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Austere conditions—严酷/极简的资源环境，指资金、人力或基础设施极度受限的状态。
Grow accustomed to—因长期暴露于某一刺激而逐渐失去其冲击感，常用于描述组织对慢性压力或常态危机的适应性机制。
Punctuated by—以周期性事件为节点，用于商业叙事中突出关键里程碑或间歇性改善（如季度复盘、技术迭代）。
Temporary reprieve—短暂的缓解，指结构性问题未解时的阶段性应对，常用于项目管理、危机公关或战略规划语境。
Stow away / be stowed—妥善收纳、置于备用，引申为资源与资产的弹性配置思维。
语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

这三段文字依次展开：先是空间的框定，然后是生存的体系，再是日常生活的节奏——这正是传记写作的经典递进：先写肖像，再写环境，最后写习惯。读者跟随一种视角，从静止移向流动，从外在场景深入内在生命。The three paragraphs move through spatial framing, systems of survival, and the rhythms of daily life—a classic biographical progression of portrait, environment, and habit. The reader follows a perspective that shifts from stillness to motion, from the outer scene to the inner life.

整段文字没有任何感叹或主观评判，叙事完全依靠事实本身的密度推进。那句“第二天早上总会出现几处红点，但那一夜他照常睡得安稳”，用生理记录替代了情绪渲染——这正是艾萨克森式传记的做法：让事实自己说话。The entire piece contains neither interjections nor subjective judgments; the narrative is carried by the sheer density of facts. The line “The next morning there would always be a few red spots, but that night he slept as soundly as usual” substitutes a physiological record for emotional coloring—an approach that fits the Isaacson school of biography, where facts are allowed to speak for themselves.

“两个世界”这一说法构建起一个跨越时代的参照框架，既让历史的纹理更加厚重，也为当代读者提供了一个可以把握、可以栖身的认知锚点。The phrase “two worlds” establishes a frame of reference that spans the ages, deepening the texture of history while giving contemporary readers a cognitive anchor they can grasp and inhabit.

School life was highly regimented. The wake-up bell rang at 6 a.m., and twenty minutes later we assembled on the playground for morning exercises, followed by breakfast. Classes ran from 8 to noon. After a thirty-minute rest following lunch, classes resumed until 4:30 p.m., when students were free. Most headed to the playground for basketball or stayed in the classroom to study; some simply talked with classmates. Dinner was at 6 p.m., and from 7 to 9 we were required to study in the classroom; lights out came with a bugle at 9:30. Before exams, some students would secretly light candles in their dorms and pull all-nighters, though it was against the rules.

那个时候的局势，最后胜利看来已不是问题，中国在国际的地位，也自珍珠港事变后，迅速地晋升为"四强"之一。我入南开后不久，蒋主席(当时蒋介石是国民政府主席)参加开罗会议，与罗斯福总统、邱吉尔首相平起平坐。消息传来，更使国人鼓舞，大家都认为中国人被列强欺负了百余年，现在终有出头的日子了，此后国家建设大业就在我们年轻一代的肩上。

段落之间潜藏着一条层层递进的“溯源”线索：从一次私人的音乐启蒙，到校园里亲手创办壁报的公共实践，再到数十年后回望校训时那一瞬的恍然大悟，最终收束于战争胜利后举国沸腾的狂欢。叙述的节奏由微小的情感颗粒——一首诗、一次造访、一页泛黄的回忆——逐步放大为历史的宏大潮汐，再用杜甫的诗句将个人命运与时代洪流缝合在一起。钱氏的独白克制而深沉，尤其在“允公允能”的顿悟时刻，他以自我否定来彰显教育力量的深邃：自己总结出的十条经营哲学，竟然全然不出那八个字的范畴。这是典型的艾萨克森式“揭示性时刻”——不靠渲染，而靠一种平静的自我承认，让思想完成对灵魂的照亮。 修辞层面，古典诗词的互文悄然嵌入，杜诗映照的是抗战胜利后的喜悦；隐喻对照巧妙分野，“十条理念”与“八字校训”之间形成的包含关系，因反差而更具张力；而自我否定式的顿悟，则让教育影响那“无形之深”获得了可触可感的形状。逻辑上以归纳为骨架，从具体的人与事出发，一步步上升到对教育本质的体认。整段叙述看似克制，实则暗涌着强烈的价值认同，恰如那些最深沉的力量——从不喧哗，却早已改变了一个人的一生。The passages form a progressive “archeological” structure: from a private musical initiation, to the public practice of founding a campus wall newspaper, to the epiphany decades later of revisiting the school motto, and finally to the collective catharsis of a nation celebrating wartime victory. The narrative rhythm expands from intimate emotions—a poem, a visit, a page of memory—to the sweep of historical events, then uses Du Fu’s verse to stitch personal fate into the current of an era. Qian’s monologue is restrained and profound, especially at the epiphany of “Yungong Yuneng,” where his self-negation—his ten business philosophies amounting to no more than the scope of those eight characters—exposes the true depth of education’s influence, a quintessential Isaacson-style “revelatory moment.” Rhetorically, it interweaves classical poetry through intertextuality (Du Fu’s lines mirroring the joy of victory in the War of Resistance), metaphorical contrast (the containment of the “ten principles” within the “eight-character motto”), and a self-negating epiphany, giving tangible form to the “invisible depth” of educational influence. Logically, the passage is predominantly inductive, rising from concrete human experience to a recognition of education’s essential nature, with restrained narration carrying a powerful undercurrent of value affirmation.

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text
**张伯苓（1876–1951）**：南开系列学校创办人，中国近代教育史上的重要人物，与严修共同倡导现代教育，提出"允公允能"的育人理念。 **Zhang Boling (1876–1951)**: Founder of the Nankai school system and a pivotal figure in modern Chinese educational history. Together with Yan Xiu, he championed modern education and proposed the educational philosophy of "Dedication to the Public Good and the Cultivation of Ability."
**西南联大**：抗战时期由北京大学、清华大学、南开大学迁至昆明合并组成的大学，在极艰苦条件下培养了杨振宁、李政道等多位诺贝尔奖得主。 **National Southwestern Associated University**: Established during the War of Resistance against Japan, this university was formed in Kunming by the merger of Peking University, Tsinghua University, and Nankai University. Despite extremely harsh conditions, it nurtured numerous Nobel laureates, including Yang Chen-Ning and Tsung-Dao Lee.
**杜甫《闻官军收河南河北》**：被誉为"杜甫生平快诗第一首"，描写的是安史之乱平息后的喜悦，钱氏以此映照抗战胜利时重庆市民的心情，古今呼应。 **Du Fu's "Recovering the Regions North and South of the Yellow River"**: Hailed as "the first joyous poem of Du Fu's life," this work captures the elation following the suppression of the An Lushan Rebellion. Qian evokes it to mirror the mood of Chongqing citizens upon victory in the War of Resistance, creating a resonance between ancient and modern times.

语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

文本以时间与因果两条线索并行推进，先勾勒出一条清晰的转学轨迹——从圣约翰附中到南模，随后落在一个耐人寻味的洞察上：两校虽行政各自独立，升学路径却高度重合。正是这一事实，让“戏称交大附中”的民间标签自然而然地生长出来。数十年后，叙述者以校友身份归来，完成了从非正式昵称到制度性接纳的反差收束，既有幽默的余味，又在中国教育的语境中悄然映照出“附属校品牌溢价”的现实逻辑。中英双语并置之际，英文保留了原文的克制与客观，中文则多了叙事的温度，以及身份认同层层递进的韵致。The passage proceeds along twin tracks—one temporal, one causal—first tracing the transfer route (St. John's Affiliated Middle School → Nanyang Model High School), then anchoring the narrative with an insight: though administratively independent, the two schools' university-admission paths largely coincide. From this, the folk label "jokingly called Jiao Tong University Affiliated High School" emerges of its own accord. The closing confirmation, decades later, of the narrator's own alumni status forms a satisfying reversal—from informal nickname to institutional embrace—at once humorous and quietly telling within the logic of "affiliated-school brand premium" that operates in Chinese education. In the bilingual pairing, the English keeps the original's restraint and objectivity, while the Chinese adds narrative warmth and a cadence of deepening identity.

外链知识窗 · Beyond the Text
**南洋模范中学**：1912年创办，上海传统名校，数理竞赛与强基计划成绩突出，与交通大学系统历史渊源深厚。 **Nanyang Model High School**: Founded in 1912, this prestigious traditional school in Shanghai has achieved outstanding results in mathematics and science competitions as well as the "Strong Foundation Plan" (China's national talent cultivation program). It shares a profound historical connection with the Jiaotong University system.
**交通大学沿革**：前身为1896年南洋公学，1921年定名交通大学；1950年代院系调整后分设为上海交大与西安交大，英文常以"China's MIT"类比其工科底蕴。 **Evolution of Jiaotong University**: Originally established as Nanyang Public School in 1896 and officially named Jiaotong University in 1921, the institution was restructured during the nationwide departmental reorganization of the 1950s, splitting into Shanghai Jiaotong University and Xi'an Jiaotong University. Its engineering pedigree is often likened to "China's MIT" in English-language discourse.
**附中文化现象**：中国高校体系中，"附属中学"多为独立法人，但因拔尖生源输送路径稳定，民间常以"XX附中"代称，形成隐性的品牌绑定与校友认同网络。 **The Affiliated School Phenomenon**: In China's higher education system, "affiliated middle schools" generally operate as independent legal entities. However, due to their well-established pathways for channeling top-tier students to affiliated universities, they are commonly referred to colloquially as "XX Affiliated School," creating an implicit brand association and alumni identity network.

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text
**徐𬣙（1908–1980）**：原名徐伯訏，浙江慈溪人，中国现代作家。其长篇小说《风萧萧》（1943年出版）是抗战时期最畅销的小说之一，以"轻轻的忧郁、淡淡的哀愁"的情调著称。文中作者对其作品推崇备至，并为其身后声名渐衰而惋惜。 **Xu Xu (1908–1980)**: Born Xu Boxun in Cixi, Zhejiang Province, he was a modern Chinese writer. His novel *The Rustling of the Wind* (published in 1943) was one of the best-selling novels during the War of Resistance against Japan, renowned for its tone of "gentle melancholy and faint sorrow." The author of this text holds his works in high esteem and laments that his reputation has gradually faded after his death.
**南模中学**：上海市南洋模范中学，由黄炎培于1911年创办，民国时期上海知名学校，以英文教育著称，多位文化名人毕业于此。 **Nanmo Middle School**: Shanghai Nanyang Model Middle School, founded by Huang Yanpei in 1911, was a prestigious school in Shanghai during the Republican era. It was known for its English education, and many prominent cultural figures were among its alumni.
**霞飞路**：上海法租界主干道，1949年后更名为淮海中路，曾是远东最繁华的商业街之一，汇聚咖啡馆、书店与西餐馆，承载老上海的城市记忆。 **Avenue Joffre**: A main thoroughfare in the French Concession of Shanghai, renamed Huaihai Middle Road after 1949. Once one of the most prosperous commercial streets in the Far East, it was lined with cafés, bookstores, and Western restaurants, embodying the urban memory of old Shanghai.

The conversation left me thoroughly unnerved, and from that moment on, the shadow of civil war hung over my thoughts.

By the second half of 1948, the war deteriorated with dizzying speed. Communist armies swept across North China and bore down aggressively on the Yangtze. That summer also brought the catastrophe of the Gold Yuan currency reform. Hyperinflation, an endemic affliction of the national economy, spiraled completely out of control, with prices multiplying several times in a single day. Until that point, citizens had been legally permitted to hold gold or US dollars to preserve their savings. But in the summer of 1948, the government revamped the monetary system, replacing the old fabi with Gold Yuan while outlawing private holdings of bullion or foreign exchange, compelling the public to surrender their assets by a strict deadline. Bereft of confidence in the new paper tender, people panicked and funneled their assets into real estate. Overnight, Shanghai property values exploded.

传记开篇便展现了艾萨克森式的镜头调度：先以微观视角凝定于十七岁少年的书桌，一个静止的瞬间；随即视野骤然拉远，推向暴风雨来临前的上海；再一路升腾，直至战局急转直下的历史大舞台。英文译文借助 harbored dreams、disabused、facade 等精准措辞，在平静表面之下暗蓄汹涌激流，营造出一种沉甸甸的历史厚重感。The narrative opens with Isaacson’s signature move—zooming in on a single, still image—the desk of a seventeen-year-old—before sweeping outward to a Shanghai poised before the storm, and then surging toward the larger stage of history as the tide of war turns. Through precise lexical choices such as *harbored dreams*, *disabused*, and *facade*, the English rendering conveys a profound historical weight beneath a deceptively calm surface.

少年时阳光灿烂的日子，与报纸上那些被许可的乐观口号，被轻轻放在天平的一端；而另一端，是父母餐桌上的低声叹息，那些见过世面的政治家与学者，在觥筹交错间吐露着对未来的隐忧，再后来，是那场当空砸下的经济崩盘。于是，世界显出它冰冷的裂缝——一边是精心编织的幻象，一边是渐渐逼近的真相。译文中的“与官方叙事截然相悖”和“步步紧逼地碾压过来”，像两道冷光彼此交错，把那种现实与幻觉互相撕扯的疼痛感照得通透。正是这种对比，让个体命运在时代巨轮的阴影下显得如此渺小而脆弱，也让整篇传记的叙事张力悄然攀至顶峰。The text sets the carefree days of youth and the “optimistic propaganda” in the newspapers against the whispered pessimism of statesmen and scholars at the family dinner table, and the economic collapse that followed. Phrases such as *sharply at odds with the state-approved narrative* and *bore down aggressively* sharpen the rupture between objective reality and subjective illusion, evoking the classic biographical tension in which vast historical forces crush individual destiny.

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text
**1948年金圆券改革（The Gold Yuan Reform of 1948）**：国民政府于1948年8月发行的法定货币，旨在收兑民间黄金、外币，以遏制因多年内战导致的严重财政赤字与法币恶性通胀。由于缺乏足够的储备金支撑且超发严重，金圆券在短短几个月内急剧贬值沦为废纸，导致城市中产阶级积蓄一空，市场经济体系全面崩溃，成为民国末期经济崩溃的核心转折点。 **The Gold Yuan Reform of 1948**: In August 1948, the Nationalist government issued a new legal tender designed to redeem private holdings of gold and foreign currency, in an effort to curb the severe fiscal deficits and runaway hyperinflation of the fabi (legal tender) wrought by years of civil war. Lacking adequate reserve backing and suffering from reckless over-issuance, the Gold Yuan note plummeted in value and was reduced to worthless paper within a matter of months. The reform drained the savings of the urban middle class and precipitated the wholesale collapse of the market economy, marking the pivotal turning point in the economic disintegration of the late Republic of China.
**民国沙龙文化与行宪立法委员（Republican Salons and the Legislative Yuan）**：民国时期的上层知识分子与政要常以家庭晚餐（Salon）的形式纵论国事。文中提到的"立法委员"系指1948年通过行宪选举产生的首届立法委员。这一群体处于政治决策与信息传播的核心圈层，他们在私人场合对战局的悲观预判，反映了当时统治精英阶层对局势失去信心的真实心态。 **Republican-Era Salon Culture and the Legislative Yuan**: During the Republican period, upper-class intellectuals and political dignitaries frequently gathered over family dinner salons to discourse at large on matters of state. The "legislative members" referenced in the text denote the inaugural cohort of the Legislative Yuan elected through the constitutional elections of 1948. Positioned at the very core of political decision-making and the dissemination of information, this circle's pessimistic assessments of the war situation in private settings laid bare the genuine loss of confidence that had taken hold among the ruling elite of the time.

My parents sank into deep despair during this period; years of hopes and dreams were shattering before their eyes. Worse, this flight would be profoundly different from the past. When fleeing the Japanese invasion, we had held fast to the conviction of eventual victory; this time, we had no idea when—if ever—we might return. My father initially inclined toward remaining, but after conferring with close friends and weighing every variable, he concluded that staying carried far too great a risk. Bound by his official duties, he could not leave immediately, so he arranged for my grandmother, my mother, and me to depart first. Carrying a few pieces of hand luggage, we boarded a steamer bound for Hong Kong. By the time we left, panic had spread and people were scrambling to flee. My father managed to secure three tickets only with great difficulty, leaving the three of us packed into a small, cramped cabin. In December 1948, with heavy hearts, we returned to Hong Kong—the city where I had spent five joyful years of my childhood. My mother and I had been away for six full years, years that had taken us through occupied Shanghai and wartime Chongqing.

Capital flight—因地缘政治风险、战乱或恶性通货膨胀，资金、财产及高净值人群大规模离开某一经济体系的现象。
Downside risk mitigation—在面对极度不确定的市场或政治环境时，通过提前清仓、转移阵地或对冲策略来尽可能降低潜在损失。
语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

译文采用了沃特·艾萨克森式的史实叙事笔法，将青年学子纵酒放歌的烂漫（黄浦江夜航上的隔水喊话）与骤然压顶的历史转折（徐蚌会战、金圆券崩溃）紧密编织在一起。*fever dream*（狂热的虚妄之梦）、*impending confrontation*（即将来临的摊牌）等英文表达携带着精确的历史分量，精准捕捉了旧秩序瓦解前夜浮华与危机并存的张力。The translation employs a Walter Isaacson-like narrative of historical fact. It tightly interweaves the youthful exuberance of students (calling out across the Huangpu River on a night voyage) with the abrupt, overwhelming historical turn (the Battle of Xubang, the collapse of the gold yuan). English renderings such as *fever dream* and *impending confrontation* carry precise historical weight, capturing the tension between glitter and crisis on the eve of the old order's dissolution.

原文“上海如醉如梦，是我们醉了？还是上海醉了？”被译作 *Shanghai glittered in the distance like a fever dream. Were we drunk, or was Shanghai itself intoxicated?* 译文巧妙地把青春的醉意转喻为一座城市正走向恶性通胀与战火崩塌的命运；而房地产“一夕上涨几倍”却“一下子跌到原来价格以下”，则以 *vaulted*（腾空跃升）与 *plummeted*（重挫直下）这对反差强烈的动词，渲染出投机泡沫破裂的极致讽刺。The original line, "Shanghai was like a drunken dream—were we drunk, or was Shanghai itself drunk?" is rendered as *Shanghai glittered in the distance like a fever dream. Were we drunk, or was Shanghai itself intoxicated?* This deftly turns youthful intoxication into a metaphor for a city heading toward hyperinflation and the collapse of war; and the real estate that "vaulted several-fold in a single night" only to "plummet below its original price" uses the starkly contrasting verbs *vaulted* and *plummeted* to evoke the intense irony of a speculative bubble bursting.

描写离别与逃难时，译文避开了过度的感伤化（bathos），转而选用 *profoundly different*、*deep despair*、*cramped cabin* 等老派文学中精准的名词与形容词。这种“低调陈述”反而强化了主人公一家直面时代巨浪时那份浸润着教养与尊严的沉痛。In depicting farewell and flight, the English avoids excessive sentimentality (bathos), instead employing precise old-fashioned literary nouns and adjectives such as *profoundly different*, *deep despair*, and *cramped cabin*. This understatement paradoxically reinforces the anguish—marked by cultivation and dignity—with which the protagonist's family confronts the immense waves of the era.

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text
沪江大学（University of Shanghai）：创建于1906年，前身为上海浸会大学，是由美国南北浸会差会联合创办的著名教会大学。其校园位于上海杨树浦军工路（现为上海理工大学校区），以优美的哥特式建筑群和沿江风光著称。民国时期，沪江大学的商科、银行学及商电专业在沪上享有盛誉，是当时中国顶级的高等商科学府之一。 University of Shanghai: Founded in 1906 as Shanghai Baptist College, it was a renowned Christian university jointly established by the Northern and Southern Baptist missions of the United States. Its campus, located on Jungong Road in Yangshupu, Shanghai (now the campus of the University of Shanghai for Science and Technology), was celebrated for its elegant Gothic architecture and riverside scenery. During the Republican era, its commerce, banking, and business correspondence programs enjoyed a distinguished reputation in Shanghai, making it one of China's premier institutions for higher business education at the time.
1948年金圆券币制改革与徐蚌会战：1948年8月，国民政府为应对全面通货膨胀，推出“金圆券”替代法币，强制收兑民间黄金、外币，一度造成虚假的物价稳定与资产飙升；然而随着同年11月国共两军在徐州、蚌埠一带展开决定性决战（即徐蚌会战/淮海战役），战局急转直下，金圆券信用彻底崩溃，引发恶性通胀与全国性资产贬值，导致当时大批上海市民倾家荡产并掀起向南方及香港逃难的潮涌。 The 1948 Gold Yuan Certificate Reform and the Battle of Xubang: In August 1948, in response to runaway inflation, the Nationalist government introduced the Gold Yuan certificate to replace the fabi, forcibly converting private gold and foreign currency. This briefly produced an illusion of price stability and surging asset values. However, when the decisive confrontation between Communist and Nationalist forces around Xuzhou and Bengbu—known as the Battle of Xubang, or the Huaihai Campaign—turned sharply against the government in November of that year, the Gold Yuan certificate collapsed entirely. Hyperinflation and nationwide asset devaluation followed, ruining countless Shanghai residents and triggering a massive wave of refugees fleeing southward and to Hong Kong.

离开战时的重庆，回到承平的上海，现在又避难回到香港。只有17岁的我，竟已油然起饱历沧桑之感。到香港几天后就是圣诞节，平常不大去教堂的母亲和我，那天也去做礼拜，我们祈祷父亲的安全，祈祷我们能早日回上海。香港幽美如昔，战后人口反而减少。那时大陆变色，难民正在大量涌入，但1948年底，总人口仍只有百万余，只是现在的五六分之一。浅水湾、山顶景色如旧，又成为我家喜爱的游憩之地，但是心情已经少了童年的那份轻松愉快了。

From wartime Chongqing to a fleetingly peaceful Shanghai, and now exiled once more to Hong Kong—at just seventeen, I felt a quiet, heavy sense of world-weariness settle over me. A few days after our arrival came Christmas. Though my mother and I rarely attended church, we went to service that day to pray: first for my father's safety, and then for a swift return to Shanghai. Hong Kong retained its quiet grace, its population surprisingly diminished after the war. Though refugees were beginning to pour in as the political tide turned on the mainland, by the end of 1948 the colony held barely a million souls—a fraction of its modern density. Repulse Bay and Victoria Peak remained the family's customary retreats, yet the unburdened innocence of my childhood visits had vanished.

我们到香港一个多月后，父亲也来到香港，一家又团聚了。父亲离开上海时，上海已是危城；两三个月后，共产党占领上海。此后更是如秋风扫落叶，不到1949年年底，大陆全部落于共产党之手。

ReadShift 双语翻译

A little over a month after our arrival, my father managed to join us, reuniting our fragile household. Shanghai had been a besieged city when he escaped; within two or three months, it fell to the Communists. What followed was a swift, overwhelming sweep across the mainland, and by the end of 1949, the entire country was lost.

回上海已遥遥无期A Return to Shanghai, Far Beyond Reach

在上海的最后几星期，全家忙着逃难，根本无暇想到未来的问题。到了香港，我的第一个大忧虑又是求学问题。我过去的计划已经落空，不但回上海重入大学遥遥无期，而且经过大陆政治、经济体制的改变，读商科还有前途吗？父亲到了香港以后，就很坚决地认为我必须读理工，毕业后才能谋生。

During our final weeks in Shanghai, swallowed by the chaos of flight, we had no time to contemplate the future. Only in Hong Kong did the question of schooling force its way back to the foreground. My original plans had collapsed entirely: returning to university in Shanghai was beyond reach, and with the political and economic transformation of the mainland, what future did a business education hold? Upon his arrival in Hong Kong, my father took a firm position: I must study science or engineering, the only fields that could guarantee a livelihood after graduation.

到哪里去读理工呢？香港那时只有一个香港大学，非但理工不强，而且整个学校也不太被看好。在逼不得已下，父亲认为我只有一条路：去美国读大学，他还有能力供给我第一年的学杂费和生活费。至于一年以后，要看他在香港的情况如何，而且我在比较习惯美国环境以后，应该可以申请奖学金，或半工半读。母亲很坦白地对我说，即使是我第一年的费用，对父亲来说已是一个沉重的负担，"幸而你是独子，不然我们不会有能力送你出国。"就在这样情形下，父母亲决定送我出国了。三叔张思侯先生那时已在波士顿东北大学任教授，他替我选择申请入哈佛大学。

But where could I study engineering? Hong Kong then had only one university, which was weak in the sciences and not highly regarded on the whole. Driven into a corner, my father saw only one path: I would go to college in America. He could afford the tuition and living expenses for my first year; for the year after, everything depended on how he fared in Hong Kong, and on my winning a scholarship or working part-time once I had grown accustomed to America. My mother told me frankly that even that first year's expenses were a heavy burden for my father. "Thank goodness you are an only child," she said, "otherwise we would never be able to send you abroad." And so my parents decided to send me overseas. My third uncle, Mr. Chang See-hou, then a professor at Northeastern University in Boston, chose Harvard and applied on my behalf.

为什么选哈佛大学呢？第一，哈佛是举世闻名的学府，第二，哈佛在波士顿，三叔可以就近照顾我。但是波士顿还有一家也是举世闻名，而且专长理工的学校：麻省理工学院。为什么在父亲已明明告诉三叔我要读理工后，三叔还是不替我选择麻省理工呢？关于这点，我后来问三叔，他笑说："我知道的你，是在重庆南开的你，那时你热爱文科，后来我又听说你要读商科。一直到你到香港才听说要读理工。我想你应该有时间渐渐建立自己的兴趣，与其急急地把你插入非常专门的麻省理工，不如让你在哈佛有一个缓冲时期。"

ReadShift 双语翻译

Why Harvard? First, Harvard was a world-famous institution; second, it was in Boston, where my uncle could look after me. But Boston also housed another world-renowned school specializing in engineering: MIT. Why, when my father had clearly told my uncle that I was to study engineering, did he not choose MIT for me? On this point, I asked my uncle years later. He laughed and said: "The boy I knew was the one at Nankai in Chongqing, who loved the humanities. Then I heard you wanted to study business. It was not until you reached Hong Kong that I heard you wanted engineering. I thought you should have time to gradually discover your own interests, rather than being thrust hastily into the highly specialized MIT—better to let you have a transition period at Harvard first."

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Tectonic shifts—地缘政治、经济体制或技术范式发生的"地壳剥离式"剧变/根本性变革。
Pragmatic verdict—指在高度不确定的危机环境中，基于生存与现实条件做出的硬核决策。
Crucible—商业环境中常用来形容高压、高精尖且残酷竞争的培养或发展环境。
背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text
张思侯（See-Hou Chang）与波士顿学术圈：张忠谋的三叔张思侯是早期留美华裔学者中的杰出代表，曾获哈佛大学电子工程博士学位，后长期任教于波士顿东北大学（Northeastern University）。他在张忠谋1949年横渡太平洋抵美初期，不仅提供了亲情庇护，更以其深刻的教育远见引导张忠谋首选哈佛大学，而非急于进入专业性极强的工科学院。 See-Hou Chang and Boston’s Academic Circle: Morris Chang’s third uncle, See-Hou Chang, was an outstanding representative of the early generation of Chinese scholars in the United States. He earned a Ph.D. in electrical engineering from Harvard University and later taught for many years at Northeastern University in Boston. When Morris Chang first crossed the Pacific and arrived in America in 1949, his uncle not only offered him the refuge of family affection but also, with remarkable educational foresight, guided him to choose Harvard first—rather than rushing into a narrowly technical engineering school.
哈佛与麻省理工：张忠谋的双重知识底色：1949年，18岁的张忠谋进入哈佛大学，成为当年哈佛全校唯一的华人本科生。在哈佛的一年中，他广泛涉猎莎士比亚、英国文学与西方历史，养成了终身阅读历史典籍的习惯；次年（1950年），他转入麻省理工学院（MIT）攻读机械工程。这一“哈佛人文通识 + MIT顶尖工程”的复合教育背景，塑造了他日后在半导体工业界兼具商业战略视野与硬核技术洞察力的独特能力。 Harvard and MIT: The Twin Intellectual Foundations of Morris Chang: In 1949, at the age of eighteen, Morris Chang entered Harvard University, becoming the only Chinese undergraduate on campus that year. During his year at Harvard, he read widely in Shakespeare, English literature, and Western history, developing a lifelong habit of reading historical classics. The following year, in 1950, he transferred to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) to study mechanical engineering. This combined educational background—Harvard’s humanistic breadth joined with MIT’s rigorous engineering—shaped his rare ability to pair commercial strategic vision with hard-nosed technological insight throughout his later career in the semiconductor industry.

「何况，哈佛的理工科也是顶尖的，只是不如麻省理工那么专门而已。」

I spent seven months in Hong Kong, and the chief business of that time was securing a passport, a visa, and admission to Harvard. To keep my studies from falling behind, I attended a private academy. Beyond rigorously reviewing high school mathematics, physics, and chemistry, I forged several close friendships. We indulged in all the passions of youth—picnics, beach trips, movies, bridge games, late-night talks, arguments, and quick reconciliations. Those seven months evaporated quickly. At last, all paperwork was cleared, and my departure was set: July 1949, just twelve days after my eighteenth birthday. At Hong Kong's Kai Tak Airport, amid my parents' parting warnings and my classmates' fond farewells, I boarded a Pan American flight bound for San Francisco. Once airborne, I opened my journal to capture the moment:

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Transition period—在组织重组、战略转型或个人职业生涯跃迁过程中，用于调适与平稳衔接的阶段。
Foresight—对市场大势、技术演进或战略选择的敏锐预判能力。
Watershed—划定新旧时代或改变命运轨迹的关键节点。
Prestige—机构或个人因卓越历史与实力而获得的广泛认可及无形资产。
语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

此处，作者以哈佛的综合性声望对照麻省理工的专业极致，并不急于褒贬，而是借由一位银行家父亲的视野，冷静呈现某个历史时刻里，社会对两所顶尖学府认知的微妙落差。Here, the author sets Harvard’s comprehensive prestige against MIT’s specialized brilliance, refusing easy judgment. Through the eyes of a banker father, he coolly renders the subtle gap in how a particular era perceived two great institutions—prestige measured against specialization.

英文行文以“Those seven months evaporated quickly”与“pivotal watershed”点出时光之疾、历史之重，将香港七个月的琐细日常与1949年夏日的时代转折牢牢缝合，寥寥数语，却力道千钧。The English prose deploys phrases like “Those seven months evaporated quickly” and “pivotal watershed,” stitching the intricate texture of seven months in Hong Kong to the seismic shifts of a single epochal summer. Fewer words, greater force.

The collective farewell—parents, classmates—collapses into a single interior frame, and the narrative tension tightens to its purest point.

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text
张忠谋与哈佛及MIT的因缘（Morris Chang at Harvard and MIT）：文中主人公为台积电（TSMC）创始人张忠谋。1949年，年仅18岁的张忠谋作为当年全校唯一的华人学生进入哈佛大学就读大一，后于次年转入麻省理工学院（MIT）机械工程系。他在自传中多次提及，哈佛的一年为其人文素养与通识视野奠定了不可替代的底色。 Morris Chang at Harvard and MIT: The protagonist of this passage is Morris Chang, founder of TSMC. In 1949, at just eighteen years old, Chang entered Harvard College as the only Chinese student in his freshman class, then transferred the following year to the Department of Mechanical Engineering at MIT. In his memoirs, he repeatedly recalls that his single year at Harvard provided an irreplaceable foundation for his humanistic cultivation and breadth of intellectual vision.
1949年的泛美航空与启德机场（Pan Am & Kai Tak Airport, 1949）：1949年正值中国历史命运的大剧变时期，香港启德机场成为连接中国大陆、香港与西方世界的关键枢纽。当时的泛美航空（Pan American World Airways）经营着战后最具标志性的跨太平洋航线（Transpacific Route），飞往旧金山不仅是地理上的跨越，更是那一代知识精英命运转移的缩影。 Pan Am & Kai Tak Airport, 1949: The year 1949 marked a seismic shift in China's historical destiny, and Hong Kong's Kai Tak Airport became a crucial hub linking the Chinese mainland, Hong Kong, and the Western world. At the time, Pan American World Airways operated the most iconic trans-Pacific routes of the postwar era. Flying to San Francisco was not merely a geographical crossing—it was a microcosm of the momentous displacement that reshaped the lives of an entire generation of intellectual elites.

凌空而起，怅然回顾，香港已在云雾中。香港半年，真如一梦，梦中明知是梦，只觉可笑而已。然而梦后回忆，竟有十分的凄凉味。八时天色渐暗，飞行在云层之上，四顾茫然，六年前初入南开中学的乡愁，又骤然来到我心。我从未离家如此之远，也从未计划离家如此之久。如今远涉重洋，要到一个陌生的国家去，展望前途，渺茫之极，怎不令人感伤呢？几十年后读这篇纸页已黄的旧日记，当时的心情，犹如昨日。

We climbed into the sky, and looking back wistfully, Hong Kong had already vanished into the clouds. Those half-year months in Hong Kong felt like a dream; even in the dream I knew it was a dream, and could only find it absurd. Yet in recollection after waking, the memory carried a distinctly desolate flavor. At eight o'clock the sky began to darken. Flying above the clouds, surrounded by vacancy on every side, the homesickness I had felt six years earlier on first entering Nankai Middle School suddenly welled up in my heart. I had never been so far from home, and never planned to be away for so long. Now, crossing the ocean to a strange country, with the road ahead utterly obscure—how could one not be sorrowful? Reading this yellowed diary page decades later, the feelings of that day are as fresh as if they were yesterday.

许多年后回顾，18岁在香港的7个月是我人生的重要分界。我的旧世界随大陆易色而破灭，新世界正待和千百万与我相似年纪的青年一样，一心预备在国内求学、做事；香港以后，我走上长居国外的第一步。香港以前，我想从商；香港以后，开始一生的科技生涯。香港以前，父母亲是我的天地，我事事都依赖他们；香港以后，我发现父母亲已不能帮助我，我只能依靠自己了。

Looking back across the years, those seven months spent in Hong Kong at eighteen marked the great divide of my life. My old world had shattered with the political upheaval on the mainland; like millions of youths my age, I had once envisioned a life studying and working in my homeland. But after Hong Kong, I took my first step toward living abroad for good. Before Hong Kong, I aspired to enter commerce; after Hong Kong, I embarked on a lifelong career in technology. Before Hong Kong, my parents were my universe, and I depended on them for everything; after Hong Kong, I realized they could no longer shelter me—I was entirely on my own.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Watershed moment—在商业与人生规划中，特指引发根本性转向、彻底重塑后续轨迹的关键节点。
Strategic pivot—个人或企业在面临外部大环境剧变时，果断放弃原有路径，重构核心方向与能力结构的应对举措。
Radical self-reliance—在领导力语境下，指失去既有资源依托或庇护后，个体所展现出的独立决策与风险承受能力。

本段文字体现了伟大传记写作特有的张力：以个体私密的情感——泛黄的纸页日记、八时渐暗的天色、离别的愁绪——作为交响般的前奏，随即猛然切入历史巨变的重浪。第三段中，作者运用了极具爆发力的“排比对比”修辞（“香港以前……；香港以后……”）。这种克制而精准的并置，不仅勾画出个人命运在政治剧变中的断层，更完成了三重核心身份的嬗变：从国内青年到海外游子、从商业志向到科技生涯、从受庇护的孩童到独立的个体。全文无一句夸张，却在冷峻的对照之间，弥漫着历史宿命感与个体主体意识觉醒的磅礴力量。This passage exemplifies the tension of great biographical writing: it opens with the intimate emotions of a single individual—the yellowed paper diary, the darkening sky at eight, the melancholy of parting—as a symphonic prelude, then abruptly plunges into the overwhelming waves of historical transformation. In the third paragraph, the author deploys a powerfully explosive rhetorical device of parallel contrast: "Before Hong Kong...; After Hong Kong..." This restrained yet precise juxtaposition not only delineates the rupture of personal fate amid political upheaval, but also completes a triple transmutation of core identity: from a young man at home to a wanderer overseas, from commercial intentions to a life in technology, from a sheltered child to an independent self. There is no exaggeration, yet in the starkness of the contrast radiates a vast sense of historical destiny and the surging force of an individual consciousness awakening.

张忠谋与18岁的大迁徙（1949）：本段文字摘自"芯片之父"、台积电（TSMC）创始人张忠谋的自传。1949年，恰逢国共内战终局与中国现代史上最大规模的人口流动潮之一。年仅18岁的张忠谋离开上海经香港赴美，考入哈佛大学（后转学至麻省理工学院）。这一代因战乱被迫"远涉重洋"的留美华人青年，后来构成了20世纪后半叶硅谷与全球半导体产业最核心的工程师与企业家群体之一。这篇日记不仅记录了他个人"科技生涯"与"独立生存"的起点，亦是那一整代中国知识分子命运转折的微缩史诗。 This passage is excerpted from the autobiography of Morris Chang, the "father of the chip" and founder of TSMC. In 1949, at the twilight of the Chinese Civil War and amid one of the largest population movements in modern Chinese history, the eighteen-year-old Chang left Shanghai for Hong Kong and then set sail for the United States, where he was admitted to Harvard University (later transferring to MIT). This generation of young Chinese students, forced by war to "cross the seas," would go on to constitute one of the most essential groups of engineers and entrepreneurs in Silicon Valley and the global semiconductor industry in the latter half of the twentieth century. This diary entry not only records the starting point of his "technological career" and "independent survival," but also serves as a miniature epic of the fateful transformation of an entire generation of Chinese intellectuals.

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text
**1948年杜鲁门大选冷门（The 1948 Truman-Dewey Upset）**：1948年美国总统大选是美国政治史上最著名的冷门事件。《芝加哥每日论坛报》甚至在大选投票结束当晚印出了错误的大字标题《杜威击败杜鲁门》（*Dewey Defeats Truman*）。当时绝大多数民调机构和主流媒体均预测共和党候选人杜威将大胜，但杜鲁门通过著名的“搭乘火车巡回演讲攻势”（Whistle-stop tour）深入底层直面民众，最终逆风翻盘。 **The 1948 Truman-Dewey Upset**: The 1948 U.S. presidential election is one of the most famous upsets in American political history. The *Chicago Daily Tribune* even printed the erroneous banner headline “*Dewey Defeats Truman*” on the night the polls closed. At the time, nearly all polling organizations and mainstream media predicted a landslide victory for the Republican candidate, Thomas Dewey. Yet Truman, through his legendary “Whistle-stop tour”—a cross-country train campaign that brought him face-to-face with ordinary citizens—staged a stunning comeback and won against all odds.
**战后美国黄金时代与GNP峰值（Post-WWII American Golden Age）**：第二次世界大战后，欧洲与亚洲主要工业国设施毁于兵燹，而美国本土未受战争波及。1940年代末期，人口仅占全球5%的美国拥有全球近半数的制造业产能与40%的GNP，造就了20世纪中叶庞大的美国中产阶级崛起与郊区住宅化（Suburbanization）浪潮。 **Post-WWII American Golden Age**: After the Second World War, the industrial infrastructure of major European and Asian powers lay in ruins, while the American homeland remained untouched by the conflict. By the late 1940s, the United States—home to just 5 percent of the world’s population—possessed nearly half of global manufacturing capacity and accounted for 40 percent of the world’s GNP. This extraordinary economic dominance fueled the rise of a vast American middle class and the great wave of suburbanization in the mid-twentieth century.
**新闻媒介的“电视化转向”（The Shift from Print to Television）**：文中提到的“电视将新闻皮毛化”预示了后来的媒介批判理论。从1950年代起，电视取代报刊成为大众获取信息的主渠道，政客政治竞选也从深入的文告阐述转向了视觉形象与声音片段（Soundbites）的博弈，深刻改变了现代公众生活与政治生态。 **The Shift from Print to Television**: The observation that “television would reduce news to mere surface” foreshadowed later media criticism. Beginning in the 1950s, television replaced newspapers as the primary source of information for the general public. Political campaigning likewise shifted from in-depth written policy statements to a contest of visual imagery and soundbites, profoundly transforming modern public life and the political landscape.

至于“只要努力，你就能出头”的理想，这似乎是一般人民共同的信仰。事实上，当时美国人的勤奋习惯远超过今日，在各行各业中，多的是白手起家、奋斗成功的例子。

**鲍勃·多尔（Bob Dole, 1923–2021）与1996年大选**：多尔为美国堪萨斯州共和党资深参议员、二战英雄，曾在意大利战场身负重伤。1996年大选中，73岁的多尔代表共和党挑战比他年轻23岁的比尔·克林顿。克林顿在大选中提出了著名口号“建立一座通往21世纪的桥梁”（Building a bridge to the 21st century），成功地将多尔的怀旧叙事定义为“退回过去”。 **Bob Dole (1923–2021) and the 1996 Election**: Dole was a veteran Republican senator from Kansas and a World War II hero who had been severely wounded in the Italian campaign. In the 1996 presidential election, the 73-year-old Dole ran as the Republican nominee against Bill Clinton, who was 23 years his junior. Clinton's famous campaign slogan, "Building a bridge to the 21st century," effectively framed Dole's nostalgic narrative as a retreat to the past.
**埃玛·拉扎勒斯与《新巨像》（Emma Lazarus & "The New Colossus"）**：该诗写于1883年，为筹集自由女神像基座修建资金而作。1903年，诗篇被刻在自由女神像基座内部的铜牌上。“Give me your tired, your poor...”这一名句成为了美国作为移民避风港、机会之地与自由灯塔的核心文化象征。 **Emma Lazarus & "The New Colossus"**: Written in 1883 to help raise funds for the pedestal of the Statue of Liberty, the poem was inscribed on a bronze plaque inside the pedestal in 1903. Its famous lines—"Give me your tired, your poor..."—became a defining cultural symbol of the United States as a haven for immigrants, a land of opportunity, and a beacon of liberty.

A few days later, I boarded a transcontinental train bound for Boston; after a two-day journey, I stepped onto the platform to find my uncle's entire family waiting to welcome me.

三叔那时36岁，他是上海交通大学电机系的高材生，毕业时全班第二名，毕业后在北平清华大学任教。抗战爆发后，迁重庆，又在重庆九龙坡交通大学任教。当父母亲和我到重庆时，他已升任为交大教授，但他仍以从未出国深造为憾。于是，在抗战胜利后的1945年底，当有机会出国时，他毫不犹豫地决定暂离三婶和小孩，独自远涉重洋到哈佛读博士。不到一年，他就完成博士学位，又因为在中国已有相当教学经验，获得博士学位后，就被聘为美国东北大学教授。三婶和三个堂妹也在1948年初到美国定居。

My third uncle was then thirty-six, a star graduate of Shanghai Jiao Tong University's electrical engineering department, where he had finished second in his class before taking up a faculty position at Tsinghua University in Peiping. When the war broke out, he relocated to Chongqing to teach at Jiao Tong's wartime campus in Jiulongpo. By the time my parents and I reached the wartime capital, he was already a full professor, yet he carried an enduring regret: he had never studied abroad. Thus, in late 1945, with victory achieved and the sea lanes reopened, he seized the opportunity without hesitation, leaving behind his wife and children to cross the ocean for a doctorate at Harvard. He swept through the program in under a year. Thanks to his rich academic background in China, he was promptly recruited as a professor at Northeastern University. His wife and three daughters joined him in America early in 1948.
