语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

**人物三角的互补结构**：张忠谋精准总结了英特尔"黄金三人组"（Noyce-Moore-Grove）的性格与角色分工——魅商并重（Noyce）、洞察务实（Moore）、严明纪律（Grove），展示了顶级科技企业早期领导班子的完美生态。 **投资复利的具象化**：从最初每人24.5万美元、占股12.25%，到2018年摩尔85亿美元身家，以简洁清晰的数字对比呈现风险投资与股权激励的巨大威力。 **宿敌交锋的宏大叙事**：段落结尾将个人履历与硅谷传奇交织——张忠谋在1972–1978年掌管德仪半导体集团期间，将英特尔视为最大对手，为后续台积电的竞争与合作埋下伏笔。**The complementary structure of the character triangle**: Chang precisely summarizes the temperaments and division of roles within Intel's "golden trio" (Noyce–Moore–Grove) — charm and business acumen in Noyce, insight and pragmatism in Moore, strict discipline in Grove — displaying the perfect ecology of a top-tier technology company's early leadership. **Making investment compounding concrete**: From an initial $245,000 each for a 12.25 percent stake to Moore's $8.5 billion fortune in 2018, crisp numerical contrasts reveal the immense power of venture capital and equity incentives. **The grand narrative of rival clashes**: The passage's close weaves personal biography into Silicon Valley legend — while Chang headed TI's Semiconductor Group from 1972 to 1978, he regarded Intel as his greatest rival, laying the groundwork for TSMC's later competition and cooperation with it.

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text
**快捷半导体与"叛逆八帮人"**：1957年诺伊斯、摩尔等八位年轻科学家离开肖克利半导体公司创立快捷半导体（Fairchild），开创了硅谷初创企业与风险投资的现代模式。 **Fairchild Semiconductor and the "Traitorous Eight"**: In 1957, eight young scientists led by Noyce and Moore left Shockley Semiconductor to found Fairchild Semiconductor, pioneering the modern model of Silicon Valley startups and venture capital.
**创投先驱阿瑟·洛克（Arthur Rock）**：硅谷最早的专业风险投资家之一，曾资助快捷半导体，后主导投资英特尔与苹果公司，是现代 Venture Capital 机制的奠基人。 **Arthur Rock, pioneer of venture capital**: One of Silicon Valley's earliest professional venture capitalists; he backed Fairchild Semiconductor and later led investments in Intel and Apple, and is a founder of the modern venture capital mechanism.
**英特尔管理三巨头**：诺伊斯（外交与构想）、摩尔（技术与预测）、葛洛夫（运营与偏执管理），三人互补管理模式被后续硅谷公司广泛效仿。 **Intel's management triumvirate**: Noyce (diplomacy and vision), Moore (technology and prediction), and Grove (operations and paranoia-driven management); their complementary management model was widely emulated by later Silicon Valley companies.

外链知识窗

**英特尔的创办（1968年）**：最初名为 NM Electronics（Noyce-Moore Electronics），后更名为 Intel（Integrated Electronics 缩写），开启了微处理器时代。 **The founding of Intel (1968)**: Initially named NM Electronics (Noyce-Moore Electronics), it was later renamed Intel (short for Integrated Electronics), ushering in the microprocessor era.
**张忠谋与英特尔的交集**：在德仪时期是市场赛道上的正面强敌；到了台积电时期，英特尔既是晶圆代工竞争者，也是其重要客户与行业标杆。 **The intersection of Morris Chang and Intel**: During his TI years they were head-on rivals on the market track; in the TSMC era, Intel was both a foundry competitor and an important customer and industry benchmark.

台湾半导体业的机会The Opportunity for Taiwan's Semiconductor Industry

一、半导体的"弥漫性"The Pervasiveness of Semiconductors

30余年前，当集成电路的高功能、低体积性质还没有充分显示时，美国海格底（美国德州仪器公司总裁）氏就首倡半导体弥漫论。

ReadShift 双语翻译

More than thirty years ago, when the high functionality and compact size of integrated circuits had yet to fully manifest, Patrick Haggerty, then president of Texas Instruments, first advanced the thesis of semiconductor pervasiveness.

他的意思是：在20世纪内，半导体因其特殊性能，必定"弥漫"（pervade）国防、工商业、民生各种用途。如今20世纪尚未结束，而海氏的远见已经实现。环顾我们周围，几乎无处没有半导体。半导体的踪影可发现在工厂（各种控制器）、商店（终端机、信用卡扫描器等等）、办公室（个人电脑、各种办公室电子用具）、家庭（电视机、各种家用电器、汽车），甚至于人身上（液晶表、移动电话）。更有甚者，半导体市场并没有接近饱和的现象，新的用途仍层出不穷。

ReadShift 双语翻译

His argument was that within the twentieth century, by virtue of their special properties, semiconductors would inevitably "pervade" every kind of use — national defense, industry, commerce, and daily life. The twentieth century has not yet ended, and Haggerty's foresight has already been fulfilled. Look around us: there is hardly a place without semiconductors. Their traces can be found in factories (all manner of controllers), shops (point-of-sale terminals, credit-card scanners, and so on), offices (personal computers and assorted office electronics), homes (televisions, household appliances, automobiles), and even on people themselves (liquid-crystal watches, mobile phones). What is more, the semiconductor market shows no sign of approaching saturation; new applications continue to emerge without end.

就以个人电脑（它只是半导体的应用之一）而言，最近方兴未艾的多媒体发展，可使个人电脑更深入办公室与家庭，当然也同时更加强了半导体的普及性。过去30年间，世界半导体市场的平均成长率为每年15%。前瞻未来10至15年，成长率仍可维持在每年15%左右。这样高幅度的持续成长是非常惊人的。它相当于每5年增加一倍，亦即是说，15年后世界半导体市场应为现在的8倍。当然，超于水准的业者应有更快速的成长。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Take the personal computer — only one application of semiconductors. The multimedia trend, just now gaining momentum, will carry PCs ever deeper into offices and homes, and of course further strengthen the pervasiveness of semiconductors. Over the past thirty years, the world semiconductor market has grown at an average annual rate of 15 percent. Looking ten to fifteen years ahead, the growth rate should hold at about 15 percent a year. Such sustained high growth is astonishing: it means doubling every five years — that is, fifteen years from now the world semiconductor market should be eight times its present size. Of course, above-average players should grow even faster.

二、台湾的机会Taiwan's Opportunity

台湾半导体业在过去10多年有远超于世界水准的表现，从10多年前的筚路蓝缕，到今年（1994年）的产值应可达30亿美元。以产值言，台湾已在世界五六名之内。这样的成就在短短10多年内发生，绝非偶然，主要是基于台湾的各种优势因素。如果我们能保持、甚至扩大这些优势因素，则今日的成就只是一个开始而已，未来的机会仍无可限量。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Over the past decade and more, Taiwan's semiconductor industry has performed far above the world standard — from the hard beginnings of a decade ago to an output value this year (1994) that should reach US$3 billion. In terms of output value, Taiwan now ranks within the world's top five or six. Such an achievement, reached in barely a decade, is no accident; it rests chiefly on Taiwan's various advantageous factors. If we can maintain — even expand — those advantages, today's achievements are only a beginning, and the opportunities ahead remain boundless.

笔者认为下列的台湾优势因素，是过去造成台湾半导体业成功的主因，也提供了未来台湾的机会：（一）技术人才充沛——半导体是一个技术密集产业。在一个典型半导体公司内，"间接人工"数目往往超过直接作业员，而"间接人工"内，绝大部分又是工程人员。所以在一个半导体公司内，具有理工学士学历以上的人员，往往占全公司人员30%以上。台湾的大学平均水准很高，而主修理工的百分比又较西方国家为高，造成相当充沛的技术人才来源。还有一点值得提出的，在美国从事半导体业的人员中，来自台湾的数以万计。这些具有工作经验的人才，在过去几年已有若干返台工作，但留在美国的更多。无庸讳言的，这是未来台湾半导体业的一个重要人才资源。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In my view, the following advantages of Taiwan are the main causes of its past success and also constitute its future opportunity: (1) An abundant supply of technical talent. Semiconductors are a technology-intensive industry. In a typical semiconductor company, the number of "indirect workers" often exceeds that of direct production operators, and the great majority of those indirect workers are engineers. Thus, in a semiconductor company, staff with a bachelor's degree or above in science or engineering often account for more than 30 percent of total employment. Taiwan's universities maintain a high average standard, and the percentage of students majoring in science and engineering is higher than in Western countries, producing a quite ample source of technical talent. There is one more point worth raising: tens of thousands of the people working in the American semiconductor industry come from Taiwan. In recent years a number of these experienced professionals have returned to work in Taiwan, but far more remain in the United States. Without question, this is an important talent resource for Taiwan's semiconductor future.

语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

**预测—验证叙事结构**：文章以"海格底先提出弥漫论，再回顾其应验"为开场，构成一种**回溯性确认**的说服逻辑——既然过去预测已被证实，则未来推论同样可信。 **指数增长的数字节奏**："每五年翻一番，十五年后达八倍"以三段递进（1→2→4→8）呈现，将抽象的15%复合成长率转化为可直观想像的扩张图景，增强论点的冲击力。 **先破后立的因果过渡**："绝非偶然"否定随机性，紧接"主要基于……优势因素"建立因果链条，是典型的事业成功叙事手法，既排除运气成分，又为后续论证铺路。 **留白式收尾**："还有其他……"刻意不完整，呼应传记笔法中的"未竟之章"风格，同时为读者延展想像、埋下悬念。 **全球化镜头对比**：从德州仪器的美国视角切入，过渡到台湾区域产业分析，形成宏观—微观的叙事张力，凸显台湾在全球半导体版图中的定位。**A predict-then-confirm narrative structure**: The essay opens with "Haggerty advanced the thesis of pervasiveness first; then we look back on its fulfillment," forming a persuasive logic of **retrospective confirmation** — since past predictions have proven true, the future inference is equally credible. **The numerical rhythm of exponential growth**: "Doubling every five years, eightfold after fifteen" is presented in a three-step progression (1→2→4→8), turning an abstract 15 percent compound growth rate into a picture of expansion one can intuitively visualize, sharpening the argument's impact. **A causal transition of negation then affirmation**: "No accident" rules out randomness, and the immediate follow-up "rests chiefly on … advantageous factors" builds the causal chain — a typical success-story device that both eliminates luck from the equation and paves the way for the arguments to come. **A closing left open**: "And there are others…" deliberately incomplete, echoing the "unfinished chapter" style of biography, while extending the reader's imagination and planting suspense. **A global lens of contrast**: The essay enters from the American perspective of Texas Instruments, then shifts to a regional-industry analysis of Taiwan, creating a macro-to-micro narrative tension that highlights Taiwan's position on the global semiconductor map.

外链知识窗 · Beyond the Text
**海格底（Patrick E. Haggerty）**：德州仪器公司总裁（1958–1976），力主半导体将弥漫于国防、工商业与民生各领域，是"半导体弥漫论"的提出者。 **Patrick E. Haggerty**: President of Texas Instruments (1958–1976), he insisted that semiconductors would pervade national defense, industry, commerce, and daily life — the originator of the "thesis of semiconductor pervasiveness."
**半导体渗透率（Semiconductor Penetration Index）**：后来成为产业研究常用指标，衡量半导体在最终产品成本中的比重，台湾工研院在此领域有长期数据追踪。 **Semiconductor Penetration Index**: It later became a commonly used indicator in industry research, measuring the share of semiconductors in the cost of final products; Taiwan's Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI) has maintained long-term data tracking in this field.
**台湾半导体产值里程碑**：1994年达30亿美元仅是起点；至2020年代，台湾晶片产值已突破千亿美元规模，台积电一家即占全球先进制程出货量逾七成。 **Milestones in Taiwan's semiconductor output**: Reaching US$3 billion in 1994 was only the starting point; by the 2020s, Taiwan's chip output had surpassed the US$100 billion mark, with TSMC alone accounting for more than 70 percent of global advanced-process shipments.

（二）资本及投资意愿——半导体是一个资本密集产业。一个具有经济规模的芯片厂，需要台币两三百亿元的投资。过去几年来，台湾已有同时投资几个芯片厂的经济能力。更重要的，台湾企业家对于半导体的投资意愿，也已急剧提升。台湾企业界对半导体的投资能力及意愿，与近几年来的日本相比，形成一个强烈的对照。即使与美国比，台湾也占优势。

ReadShift 双语翻译

(2) Capital and the willingness to invest. Semiconductors are a capital-intensive industry. A chip plant of economic scale requires an investment of twenty or thirty billion New Taiwan dollars. In the past few years, Taiwan has already had the financial capacity to invest in several chip plants simultaneously. More importantly, the willingness of Taiwan's entrepreneurs to invest in semiconductors has risen sharply. Compared with Japan in recent years, Taiwan's business community presents a striking contrast in both capacity and willingness to invest in semiconductors. Even against the United States, Taiwan holds the advantage.

（三）非劳力密集——如上所述，半导体业是一个技术密集，也是一个需要大量技术人才的产业，但它不是一个劳力密集的产业。以每一员工每年营业收入来衡量，半导体业超出工业平均不少。这一产业特征，在劳工缺乏、台币升值、工资飞涨的环境下，变成一个优势。

ReadShift 双语翻译

(3) Not labor-intensive. As noted above, the semiconductor industry is technology-intensive and requires large numbers of technical talent, but it is not a labor-intensive industry. Measured by annual revenue per employee, semiconductors exceed the industrial average by a considerable margin. In an environment of labor shortage, appreciation of the New Taiwan dollar, and soaring wages, this industrial characteristic becomes an advantage.

（四）政府政策的鼓励——政府无疑是今日台湾半导体业成就的功臣。政策的鼓励，包括工研院过去的研究开发、科学园区土地与标准厂房的提供及各种服务、和对科技工业的税收优惠。

ReadShift 双语翻译

(4) Government policy support. The government is unquestionably a contributor to Taiwan's semiconductor achievements today. That support includes the Industrial Technology Research Institute's past research and development, the provision of land and standard factory buildings in the science parks with various services, and tax incentives for the technology industry.

（五）低污染——半导体业是一种低污染工业，而且现代的设备更可以把污染减到最低限度。对半导体业而言，在环保意识强烈的环境内，这是一个优势。

ReadShift 双语翻译

(5) Low pollution. The semiconductor industry is a low-pollution industry, and modern equipment can reduce pollution to the very minimum. In an environment of strong environmental awareness, this is an advantage for semiconductors.

（六）国际市场开放——半导体可说是国际贸易最为畅通的商品之一。美国、西欧市场的障碍很低，日本市场的障碍在近年来也逐渐降低。台湾本身的半导体市场很大，但开放的国际市场更增加台湾半导体业发展的空间。

ReadShift 双语翻译

(6) Open international markets. Semiconductors are among the most freely traded goods in international trade. Barriers in the American and Western European markets are very low, and barriers in the Japanese market have also been gradually lowered in recent years. Taiwan's own semiconductor market is large, but open international markets enlarge the space for Taiwan's semiconductor industry still further.

笔者认为以上所述是台湾半导体业进步的重要因素。进一步看，笔者认为这些有利因素大致仍然存在，可创造半导体业将来在台湾发展的机会。近几年来，岛内常有投资环境恶化，投资意愿低落的忧患。但是就半导体业而言，甚至可以说就科技产业而言（因为大部分适用于半导体业的有利条件，亦适用于一般科技产业），台湾仍能提供一个好的发展环境。

ReadShift 双语翻译

I believe the above are the important factors in Taiwan's semiconductor progress. Looking further, I believe these favorable factors by and large still exist, and can create opportunities for the semiconductor industry's future development in Taiwan. In recent years there has been frequent anxiety on the island about the deteriorating investment environment and flagging willingness to invest. But for semiconductors — indeed, one might say for technology industries generally, since most of the conditions favorable to semiconductors also apply to technology industries at large — Taiwan can still provide a good development environment.

三、台湾半导体业应采取的策略

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
capital-intensive industry—资本密集型产业，指需投入大量资金用于固定资产、设备与研发，而非依赖人工成本的行业。
investment appetite—投资意愿，反映企业或资本对特定领域进行资金投入的积极性与风险承受度。
economies of scale—经济规模/规模经济，指随着产量上升，单位产品成本下降的现象；达到"经济规模"即具备市场竞争力的最低产能门槛。
tax incentives—税收优惠，政府为引导资本流向特定产业或区域而提供的减税、免税或延后课税措施。
语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

本文虽为产业分析文体，但具备清晰的叙事骨架与论证节奏。作者善用**对比**（台湾与日本、美国的投资意愿对照）、**转折反转**（"非劳力密集"在缺工与币值升值背景下化为优势），以及**限定性补充**（括号内说明半导体有利条件同样适用于广义科技产业），使论述兼具学术严谨与可读性。语言克制而有力，避免情绪化修辞，符合艾萨克森式"以事实驱动叙事"的风格：将资本、政策、人才与地缘市场编织成一条逻辑链，让读者自然得出"台湾半导体具备结构性韧性"的判断。Although this passage is written as an industry analysis, it carries a clear narrative backbone and a measured argumentative rhythm. The author deftly employs **contrast** (setting Taiwan's willingness to invest against Japan's and America's), **reversal** ("not labor-intensive" turning into an advantage amid labor shortages and currency appreciation), and **qualifying additions** (the parenthetical note that conditions favorable to semiconductors apply equally to technology industries at large), giving the argument both scholarly rigor and readability. The language is restrained yet forceful, avoiding emotional rhetoric, in keeping with Isaacson's style of "narrative driven by facts": weaving capital, policy, talent, and geographic markets into a single logical chain that leads the reader naturally to the conclusion that Taiwan's semiconductor industry possesses structural resilience.

外链知识窗 · Beyond the Text
**工研院（ITRI）**：1973年创立，是台湾半导体产业的技术孵化器。其早期主导引进CMOS制程技术，并促成台积电（TSMC）于1987年分立成立，奠定了台湾代工模式的基石。 **Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI)**: Founded in 1973, it served as the technology incubator of Taiwan's semiconductor industry. In its early years it led the introduction of CMOS process technology and helped TSMC spin off in 1987, laying the cornerstone of Taiwan's foundry model.
**半导体产业周期与政策韧性**：2000年代初台湾曾担忧"产业空心化"与过度依赖半导体，但政府通过多项产业政策尝试分散风险，而半导体生态系反而因全球化分工进一步巩固。 **Semiconductor industry cycles and policy resilience**: In the early 2000s Taiwan worried about "industrial hollowing-out" and overdependence on semiconductors, and the government tried to diversify risk through a range of industrial policies — yet the semiconductor ecosystem was instead further consolidated by the global division of labor.
**推荐阅读**：Walter Isaacson, *The Innovators*（探讨技术生态如何由制度、资本与人才协同演化）；工研院院刊《台湾半导体产业的发展》专题（详述政策介入与产业跃升的关键节点）。 **Recommended reading**: Walter Isaacson, *The Innovators* (exploring how technological ecosystems evolve through the co-evolution of institutions, capital, and talent); and the ITRI journal's special issue on "The Development of Taiwan's Semiconductor Industry" (detailing the key junctures of policy intervention and industrial leap-forward).

有了有利环境和机会，台湾半导体业应采取什么策略，俾能更上一层楼呢？（一）保持生产优势——台湾半导体工厂的良率、生产率、品质一直是台湾半导体业的最大优势。近年来，台湾在设计、营销上也有大幅的进步，但生产优势无疑地仍是台湾半导体业的大本钱。要保持生产优势，必须继续开发每一代的新生产技术，投资每一代的新生产设备，并且保持高度工厂人力水准。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Given a favorable environment and opportunity, what strategy should Taiwan's semiconductor industry adopt in order to reach the next level? (1) Preserve the manufacturing advantage. The yield rates, productivity, and quality of Taiwan's semiconductor factories have always been the industry's greatest advantage. In recent years Taiwan has also made major progress in design and marketing, but the manufacturing advantage is unquestionably still the industry's biggest capital. To preserve it, Taiwan must keep developing each new generation of production technology, invest in each new generation of production equipment, and maintain a highly skilled factory workforce.

（二）世界市场是目标——上面已经说过，半导体的国际贸易甚为畅通，市场已失去国界。每一半导体公司都应以世界市场为目标。事实上许多家世界级半导体公司都各有所长，而各把自己所长的产品行销于世界市场。举例来说，日、韩公司生产大量存储器，行销于美、欧、台湾市场，而美国英特尔公司以微处理器霸主地位，大量销售微处理器于各国市场，英特尔本身需要大量的存储器，却反而向别的公司购买。这种因自由贸易而形成的分工形态，可使整个产业更为蓬勃发展，也产生了许多利基机会，可供后来进入这产业者（例如台湾）利用。

ReadShift 双语翻译

(2) The world market is the goal. As said above, international trade in semiconductors is quite free; the market has lost its national boundaries. Every semiconductor company should aim at the world market. In fact, many world-class semiconductor companies each have their own strengths and sell their specialty products in the world market. For example, Japanese and Korean companies produce large quantities of memory chips and market them in America, Europe, and Taiwan, while America's Intel, dominant in microprocessors, sells microprocessors in large volumes to markets around the world — and Intel itself needs large quantities of memory, which it buys from other companies. This pattern of specialization, born of free trade, makes the whole industry flourish more vigorously and creates many niche opportunities for latecomers such as Taiwan.

本土市场的大小，反而不是那么重要。（三）世界级的经营方式——半导体的市场和竞争是国际性的，高级人才的流通也已渐渐成为国际性。只要看近几年来有不少人才自美国流向韩国、台湾，而同时又有更多台湾人才或进入、或留在美国半导体业就可见其趋势。要吸引或留住高级人才，要在此日新月异的行业竞争，而竞争的对象又是世界级的大公司，我们必须采取世界级的经营方式。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The size of the domestic market, on the contrary, is not so important. (3) World-class management. The semiconductor market and its competition are international, and the flow of senior talent has gradually become international as well. One need only look at the many people who have moved from America to Korea and Taiwan in recent years, while still more Taiwanese have entered or remained in the American semiconductor industry, to see the trend. To attract and retain senior talent, to compete in this fast-changing industry, and to face world-class companies as competitors, Taiwan must adopt world-class management.

所谓世界级经营，当然也因应各国文化而不同，但笔者认为有几点是共通的：管理应采领导式，而非权威式；组织应采扁平型；研发应该是公司的重要工作；内部沟通应尽量开放；用人应采唯才是用原则；员工绩效应经常考核，优者奖励，劣者改进或淘汰；员工应有与股东分享利润的机会等等。

ReadShift 双语翻译

World-class management naturally differs according to each country's culture, but I believe a few points are common to all: management should be leadership-style rather than authoritarian; organizations should be flat; R&D should be an important part of the company; internal communication should be as open as possible; hiring should follow the principle of merit alone; employee performance should be regularly evaluated, with the strong rewarded and the weak improved or removed; and employees should have opportunities to share profits with shareholders — and so on.

（四）增强研究发展，并争取知识产权——以对研发的投资而言，台湾半导体业已是本土工业的佼佼者，但以世界水准衡量，台湾半导体业尚须进一步增强。研发成果之一是知识产权，先进国家的大公司因为历史因素，在今日仍享有知识财富的绝大优势，而且运用知识产权为重要竞争工具，我们必须急起直追。知识产权的累积需要时日，但5年、10年的努力，应可产生相当成绩。日本、韩国公司在近10年、15年来的成就，可作为我们的前鉴。

ReadShift 双语翻译

(4) Strengthen R&D and secure intellectual property. In terms of R&D investment, Taiwan's semiconductor industry is already outstanding among domestic industries, but measured by world standards it must be strengthened further. One fruit of R&D is intellectual property. Because of historical factors, the large companies of the advanced countries still enjoy an overwhelming advantage in knowledge assets today, and wield intellectual property as an important competitive weapon — we must hurry to catch up. Accumulating intellectual property takes time, but five or ten years of effort should produce considerable results. The achievements of Japanese and Korean companies over the past ten or fifteen years can serve as our guide and warning.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Yield rate—良率，指生产过程中良品占总产量的比例，半导体业核心指标。
Division of labor—分工，指因自由贸易而形成的各国专精领域的分工体系。
Niche opportunity—利基机会，指大企业未覆盖的细分市场空间。
Lead rather than command—领导式管理 vs 权威式管理，强调启发而非压服。
Proprietary knowledge—知识财产/专利知识，指企业独有的技术与智慧资产。
语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

本文采用"总—分"结构，四段各有主轴：生产优势→全球视野→管理模式→研发与IP，逻辑递进从"守住基本盘"到"向外扩张"再到"内部革新"，最后落脚于长期积累。作者善用对比重复（如"世界级"一词出现四次）强化主旨，并以英特尔向竞争对手购买存储器的例子具体说明"分工创造双赢"——这是艾萨克森擅长的写法：用一个反直觉的细节，让抽象理论落地。This passage follows a "general-to-specific" structure, with each of its four sections built around one central theme: manufacturing advantage → global vision → management model → R&D and IP. The logic progresses from "defending the home base" to "expanding outward" to "internal innovation," and finally settles on long-term accumulation. The author reinforces the thesis through repeated contrast (the phrase "world-class" appears four times), and uses the example of Intel buying memory chips from competitors to concretely illustrate how "specialization creates win-win outcomes" — a signature Isaacson move: grounding an abstract theory with one counterintuitive detail.

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text
**台湾半导体的"制造护城河"**：台积电（TSMC）全球先进制程市占率超过九成，其核心竞争力正是文中所说的"良率+效率+品质"铁三角，这一点在2020年代被反复验证。 **Taiwan's "manufacturing moat" in semiconductors**: TSMC commands over 90 percent of the global market share in advanced process nodes, and its core competitiveness is exactly the "yield + efficiency + quality" trinity described in the passage — a fact repeatedly vindicated through the 2020s.
**Intel 的 IDM 模式困境**：文中提到 Intel 向别人买存储器，反映出其"设计强、制造弱"的结构性矛盾，最终促使 Intel 在2020年代开放代工服务（IFS），试图重新回到全球供应链的中心。 **Intel's IDM model predicament**: The passage's mention of Intel buying memory chips from others reflects its structural tension of being "strong in design, weak in manufacturing," which ultimately pushed Intel to open its foundry services (IFS) in the 2020s in an attempt to return to the center of the global supply chain.
**日韩半导体的追赶路径**：Samsung 与 SK Hynix 在存储器领域超越台湾，关键在于它们在1980–90年代进行了长达十数年的国家级研发投入，与文末"5到10年努力"的判断完全吻合。 **The catch-up path of Japanese and Korean semiconductors**: Samsung and SK Hynix overtook Taiwan in memory chips, and the key lay in their decade-long, nationally backed R&D investment during the 1980s–90s — entirely consistent with the passage's closing judgment that "five to ten years of effort" should suffice.

外链知识窗

**半导体全球化分工格局**：美国主导芯片设计（如 Intel、NVIDIA），日韩主导存储器制造，台湾专注先进制程代工——三者形成互补而非零和的产业生态，这正是"自由贸易塑造分工形态"的现实写照。 **The global division of labor in semiconductors**: America leads chip design (e.g., Intel, NVIDIA), Japan and Korea dominate memory manufacturing, and Taiwan specializes in advanced-process foundry — together forming a complementary rather than zero-sum industrial ecosystem, a living illustration of how "free trade shapes the pattern of specialization."

（五）争取政府的继续支持——环顾半导体大国，日、韩半导体业过去受政府支持甚大；美国半导体业亦受国防研究之惠；西欧各国政府支持半导体不遗余力，但成效不彰。今日情形，日本政府对半导体业的直接支援逐渐减少，但美国政府的角色则在近几年内反趋积极。在新兴国家中，新加坡及中国大陆政府也在积极建立半导体业。台湾半导体业虽然渐具规模，但政府政策的积极支持，仍属必要。政府研发单位虽不必从事大规模的生产技术开发，但如能从事尖端技术研发，仍能帮助业者。

ReadShift 双语翻译

(5) Secure continued government support. Looking around the semiconductor powers, Japan's and Korea's industries have received enormous government support; the American industry has benefited from defense research; Western European governments supported semiconductors with all their might, but with little result. Today Japan's direct support for the semiconductor industry is gradually decreasing, while the American government's role has actually become more active in recent years. Among the newly industrializing countries, Singapore and mainland China are also actively building semiconductor industries. Though Taiwan's semiconductor industry is growing in scale, active support from government policy is still necessary. Government research units need not undertake large-scale production technology development, but if they engage in frontier technology research, they can still help the industry.

科学园区的角色，随着园区厂商的增加及范围的扩大，将更为吃重。土地、水、电、人力的供应，这些都是政府可以帮助半导体业的地方。（六）策略联盟——无论在研究发展上，或在厂房设备上，半导体公司的投入都越来越庞大。即使最大的半导体公司也有与其他公司联盟的必要。台湾半导体业在世界舞台上充其量是中型公司，更有结盟合作的需要。研发、生产、营销都在可合作的范围内。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The role of the science parks will grow ever heavier as the number of tenant companies and the size of the parks increase. The supply of land, water, power, and labor — these are areas where the government can help the semiconductor industry. (6) Strategic alliances. Whether in R&D or in plant and equipment, the investments of semiconductor companies are growing ever larger. Even the largest semiconductor companies find it necessary to ally with others. Taiwan's semiconductor companies are, at best, medium-sized on the world stage, and have an even greater need for alliances and cooperation. R&D, production, and marketing all fall within the scope of possible cooperation.

四、台湾半导体业的前瞻The Outlook for Taiwan's Semiconductor Industry

台湾具有充分的优良条件，世界半导体市场也呈现了一个良好的机会，笔者对于台湾半导体的发展深感乐观。今年台湾半导体产额应达30亿美元，占世界产额2.5%-3%。笔者认为台湾6年后（2000年）的目标，该是世界产额的5%，那时世界产额应在2500亿美元左右，而台湾产额目标应在125亿美元左右，亦即今年的4倍。如果现在有5个厂，6年后就要有20个厂。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Taiwan possesses ample favorable conditions, and the world semiconductor market presents a good opportunity; I am deeply optimistic about Taiwan's semiconductor development. This year Taiwan's semiconductor output should reach US$3 billion, or 2.5 to 3 percent of world output. In my view, Taiwan's goal six years from now (2000) should be 5 percent of world output; by then world output should be around US$250 billion, and Taiwan's target output should be around US$12.5 billion — four times this year's figure. If there are five plants now, there will need to be twenty plants in six years.

这样算起来，最近甚嚣尘上的许多建厂计划，即使都能如期执行，似乎还不能算多。当然，建厂只是达到目标的第一步，有了产能，还要有技术、产品、营销渠道、良好的经营。台湾半导体业是否能度过重重的挑战，就要看大家的努力了。（本文摘自《工商时报》出版的《台湾经济蓝皮书：一九九五年台湾经济与产业形势预测与分析》一书）

Calculated this way, the many plant-building plans so noisily publicized of late, even if all are executed on schedule, still do not seem to be too many. Of course, building plants is only the first step toward the goal: with capacity in hand, one still needs technology, products, marketing channels, and sound management. Whether Taiwan's semiconductor industry can weather the many challenges will depend on everyone's efforts. (Excerpted from the Taiwan Economic Blue Book: 1995 Taiwan Economic and Industrial Forecast and Analysis, published by the Commercial Times.)

发展台湾科技业Developing Taiwan's Technology Sector

前言Foreword

台湾科技业在最近十几年有很快的发展。至今，科技产业已占整个制造业的25%，也是最大出口行业。较诸20年前，或与别的东南亚及其他正在开发中国家比较，我们可以骄傲。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Taiwan's technology industry has developed very rapidly over the past decade or so. Today the technology sector already accounts for 25 percent of all manufacturing, and is also the largest export industry. Compared with twenty years ago, or with the developing economies of Southeast Asia and elsewhere, we may be proud.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
Frontier R&D—尖端技术研发。指政府或企业聚焦于技术前沿而非大规模量产的研究投入，强调"领跑"而非"跟进"。
Strategic Alliance—策略联盟。半导体行业为分摊巨额研发与建厂成本而形成的跨企业合作模式，强调结构性依存而非短期投机。
Capacity Scaling—产能扩张。从现有工厂数量向目标规模快速扩充的过程，是半导体工业化进程中的核心量化指标。
Infrastructure Enablement—基础条件支持。政府通过提供土地、水电、人才等关键生产要素，降低高技术产业的进入与运营门槛。
Disciplined Execution—良好经营/严谨运营。强调仅有产能不足，需配套技术迭代、产品定位与渠道管理的精细化落地能力。
外链知识窗 · Beyond the Text
**《台湾经济蓝皮书》**：《工商时报》出版的年度台湾经济与产业形势分析报告，《台湾半导体业的机会》一文即收录其中。 **Taiwan Economic Blue Book**: An annual analysis of Taiwan's economic and industrial conditions published by the Commercial Times; the essay "The Opportunity for Taiwan's Semiconductor Industry" is collected within it.
**1994年台湾半导体产值**：30亿美元、世界第五六名——这是台湾半导体业起飞初期的里程碑，此后二十余年产值增长超过三十倍。 **Taiwan's semiconductor output value in 1994**: US$3 billion, ranking fifth or sixth in the world — a milestone from the early takeoff of Taiwan's semiconductor industry, whose output value grew more than thirtyfold over the following two decades.

但必须认清的事实是：今日台湾科技产业仍只是技术生产工业。为什么我称它为"技术生产工业"？因为大多数的科技业专长仅在生产，虽然这生产是技术密集的生产。我们的"科技业"缺乏创新性与突破性的科技开发，也因为如此，我们的技术虽在若干领域已非常接近尖端水准，但始终不能领先。

ReadShift 双语翻译

But the fact we must recognize is that Taiwan's technology industry today is still only a technology-production industry. Why do I call it a "technology-production industry"? Because most of the technology sector's expertise lies in production alone, albeit technologically intensive production. Our "technology industry" lacks innovative and breakthrough technological development; for this very reason, although our technology is already very close to the frontier in several fields, it can never quite lead.

"技术生产工业"值得珍惜，也值得继续努力发展。它已为台湾带来不少财富，在未来十几年也会继续提高我们的经济水准，但是它的竞争障碍不够高。未来十几年中，不少国家或地区（包括大陆）也会走这条路，对我们产生竞争压力。对台湾来说，这是一个要严肃思考的问题。台湾如果要具备充分的能力来迎接、甚至进一步摆脱这种竞争压力，必须正视发展竞争障碍高的科技产业。竞争障碍最高的科技产业，是一个不断创新、不断站在科技尖端的产业。我们怎样才能创造这样的科技业？

ReadShift 双语翻译

The "technology-production industry" deserves to be cherished and developed further. It has brought Taiwan considerable wealth, and will continue to raise our standard of living in the decade or two ahead — but its competitive barriers are not high enough. In the coming ten to fifteen years, many countries and regions, including mainland China, will walk the same road and put competitive pressure on us. For Taiwan, this is a question that must be considered seriously. If Taiwan is to be fully capable of meeting — let alone escaping — such competitive pressure, it must face squarely the need to develop technology industries with high competitive barriers. The technology industry with the highest competitive barriers is one that ceaselessly innovates and stands at the technological frontier. How can we create such a technology industry?

过去的政策措施，例如设立科学园区、工研院、开发基金、税收优惠等，在促成今日的"技术生产工业"过程中，已发挥播种、奠基的功能。但如果只是继续过去的措施，最多只能增加"技术生产工业"的数量，并不能使我们冲到科技产业的尖端，也不足以让台湾建立高竞争障碍的科技业。在自由经济体制下，企业发展应该是每一企业的责任，但政府也有其必要角色。政府必须建立一个良好的文化、物质环境，使科技业能在台湾蓬勃发展。以下是我对政府角色的看法。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Past policy measures — the establishment of science parks, the Industrial Technology Research Institute, development funds, tax incentives, and so on — have played the role of sowing and laying foundations in bringing about today's "technology-production industry." But if we only continue the past measures, at most we will increase the quantity of "technology-production industry"; we will not push ourselves to the frontier of the technology sector, nor will it suffice for Taiwan to build a technology industry with high competitive barriers. Under a free-market economy, enterprise development should be the responsibility of each enterprise — but the government also has a necessary role. The government must build a good cultural and material environment so that the technology industry can flourish in Taiwan. The following are my views on the government's role.

一、基础设施Infrastructure

土地、水、电、电讯、便利的交通、员工子女学校是最基本，也是最低限度的要求。新竹科学园区除了提供这些需要外，还提供了在当时被认为优美的工作、居住环境，以及便利的单一窗口服务。新竹科学园区是台湾科技业的大功臣。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Land, water, power, telecommunications, convenient transportation, and schools for employees' children are the most basic — and minimum — requirements. Besides providing these, the Hsinchu Science Park also offered a working and residential environment considered beautiful at the time, as well as convenient one-stop services. The Hsinchu Science Park is a great contributor to Taiwan's technology industry.

现在时过17年，科技业所需的基本条件不但没有变，而且更严格。而台湾现在已富裕得多，对工作、环境的要求更高。新竹科学园区达到饱和后，政府开始规划推动台南科学园区，对已经投入科技产业，或正准备涉足科技业者是一大福音。但园区基本建设的完成是首要之急，水电供应要做到对厂商无忧虑，高铁可能带来的震动以及电磁干扰也一定要解决。园区内更须建立周详的设施。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Now seventeen years have passed; the basic conditions required by the technology industry have not only not changed, they have become stricter. Taiwan is now much wealthier, and demands more of work and environment. After the Hsinchu Science Park reached saturation, the government began planning the Tainan Science Park — a great boon for those already in the technology industry or preparing to enter it. But completing the park's basic infrastructure is the first priority: water and power supply must leave manufacturers without worry, and the vibrations and electromagnetic interference the high-speed rail may bring must be solved. Elaborate facilities must also be established within the park.

二、放松公司上市规定，允许公司授与员工股票选择权

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
advanced-production enterprise—技术密集型生产工业；强调以高技能制造为核心，但缺乏原创研发与突破能力。
competitive moat—竞争护城河/壁垒；企业在市场中抵御模仿与价格战的结构优势。
bleeding edge—科技最前沿；比"cutting edge"更具动态与风险感，暗示尚未完全成熟、需承担试错成本的领域。
single-window administrative clearance—单一窗口审批服务；政府将多项行政许可整合至统一平台，降低企业合规成本。
stock options—股票选择权/员工股权激励；允许员工以约定价格购买公司股票，常用于绑定核心人才与长期利益。
语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

**设问自答**："为什么我称它为"技术生产工业"？因为……"以作者直接发声建立论述节奏，使抽象的产业判断具象为可追踪的逻辑链，契合传记写作中"以问题驱动叙事"的惯用技法。 **隐喻克制使用**："competitive moat remains shallow"以护城河喻指竞争壁垒，既保留商业语境的专业感，又避免过度煽情；"sowing and leveling ground"以农耕意象承接政策铺垫的历史纵深，形成技术与自然演进交织的叙事质感。 **冷峻对比**：开篇肯定既有成就（"reliable engine of prosperity"），随即转入结构性隐忧（"moat remains shallow"），语调克制、不灌鸡汤，体现艾萨克森式传记对"成就与局限并置"的客观凝视。 **递进式结构**：现状诊断→危机推演→政策反思→政府职能，层层剥茧，段落间以逻辑而非情绪衔接，使论述具备工程般的精确度。**Rhetorical question answered in kind**: "Why do I call it a 'technology-production industry'? Because…" The author speaks in his own voice to establish the argumentative rhythm, rendering an abstract industrial judgment as a traceable chain of logic — a technique consistent with the "question-driven narrative" common in biographical writing. **Restrained use of metaphor**: "competitive moat remains shallow" uses the image of a moat for competitive barriers, preserving the professional tone of the business context while avoiding over-sentimentality; "sowing and leveling ground" borrows agricultural imagery to absorb the historical depth of earlier policy groundwork, producing a narrative texture where technology and natural evolution intertwine. **Cool contrast**: The passage opens by affirming existing achievements ("reliable engine of prosperity"), then pivots to structural anxieties ("moat remains shallow"); the tone stays measured and refuses to offer easy reassurance, reflecting the Isaacsonian biographical gaze that objectively juxtaposes achievement and limitation. **Progressive structure**: diagnosis of the current state → extrapolation of the crisis → reflection on policy → the government's role — peeling back each layer in turn, with sections joined by logic rather than emotion, lending the argument engineering-grade precision.

外链知识窗 · Beyond the Text
**新竹科学园区（Hsinchu Science Park）**：1980年设立，台湾第一个科学园区，被誉为"台湾硅谷"。通过土地、水电、税收与一站式服务组合，成功吸引台积电、联发科、鸿海等企业集聚，是台湾从农业社会跃升为半导体重镇的关键制度实验。[新竹科学工业园区管理局官网](https://www.hsinchu-science.gov.tw) **Hsinchu Science Park**: Established in 1980 as Taiwan's first science park, it has been hailed as "Taiwan's Silicon Valley." By combining land, water and power, tax incentives, and one-stop services, it successfully drew companies such as TSMC, MediaTek, and Hon Hai to cluster there, serving as the pivotal institutional experiment that lifted Taiwan from an agricultural society to a semiconductor powerhouse. [Hsinchu Science Park Bureau official website](https://www.hsinchu-science.gov.tw)
**工业技术研究院（ITRI）**：1973年成立，台湾技术研发的核心智库。主导了半导体、显示面板、资通讯等关键技术的引进与本土化，被誉为"台湾产业摇篮"。[工研院官网](https://www.itri.org.tw) **Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI)**: Founded in 1973, it is the core think tank of Taiwan's technology R&D. It led the introduction and localization of key technologies in semiconductors, display panels, and ICT, earning the reputation of "Taiwan's cradle of industry." [ITRI official website](https://www.itri.org.tw)
**艾萨克森传记方法论**：沃尔特·艾萨克森擅长以"技术演进史+关键人物决策"双线叙事，语言精确、克制，常将产业政策置于更长历史周期中审视。本段对"生产规模≠创新领导力"的辨析，与其在《史蒂夫·乔布斯传》中强调"创新来自跨学科交叉与制度宽容"的核心观点高度呼应。 **Isaacson's biographical methodology**: Walter Isaacson excels at a dual-track narrative of "the history of technological evolution + the decisions of key figures," with precise, restrained language that often views industrial policy within a longer historical arc. This passage's analysis that "production scale ≠ innovation leadership" closely echoes the core view he stresses in *Steve Jobs*: that innovation springs from interdisciplinary cross-pollination and institutional tolerance.

最近美国《商业周刊》报导，仅仅位在硅谷的科技公司已近一万家。美国科技业的繁荣兴旺，很大一部分原因归功于这许多"野火烧不尽，春风吹又生"的小公司。它们造成了一个"百花齐放，万家争鸣"的竞争环境。创业者的最大诱因是致富机会，而致富的正常途径是股票上市。美国法令对公司上市限制不严，但对公司营运、财务资料之及时公开，以及股市内线交易，却有严谨的规范。法令目的是保障投资人及时得知公司资料的权利，且禁止公司内部人员利用投资大众尚未知悉之资讯操作谋利。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Business Week recently reported that the technology companies located in Silicon Valley alone number nearly ten thousand. The prosperity and vigor of America's technology industry can be attributed in large part to these small companies that "survive the fire and grow again in spring." They created a competitive environment of "a hundred flowers blooming, a hundred voices contending." The greatest incentive for entrepreneurs is the chance to get rich, and the normal road to wealth is listing on the stock market. American law is not strict in restricting company listings, but it has rigorous regulations on the timely disclosure of corporate operations and financial data, and on insider trading in the stock market. The purpose of the law is to safeguard investors' right to timely information about companies, and to prohibit company insiders from profiting by trading on information the investing public has not yet learned.

法令的目的不在对上市公司是否得投资做判断。反观台湾，上市限制严格，但投资人及时获得上市公司正确资讯不易。内线交易有利少数知情人士而罔顾投资大众权益的事件也时有所闻。有关公司上市，以及上市后的监督法令之建立及执行，都值得检讨。员工股票选购权在美国是提升企业活力的重要工具。台湾证券法不允许此类选购权，许多科技公司就直接以股票分红，虽达到激励员工的目的，但有两个缺点：第一，股票分红不能把股东和员工的利益连结在一起；第二，股票分红一次全数发放，反而鼓励跳槽。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The purpose of the law is not to judge whether a listed company is worth investing in. In Taiwan, by contrast, listing restrictions are strict, but it is not easy for investors to obtain timely and accurate information about listed companies. Incidents in which insider trading benefits a few informed persons at the expense of the investing public are heard of from time to time. Both the establishment and the enforcement of laws on listing and post-listing supervision deserve review. Employee stock options are an important tool for invigorating companies in America. Taiwan's securities law does not permit such options, so many technology companies simply distribute stock dividends instead; this achieves the purpose of motivating employees, but has two drawbacks: first, stock dividends cannot bind the interests of shareholders and employees together; second, since stock dividends are distributed all at once, they actually encourage job-hopping.

三、尖端研发Cutting-Edge R&D

尖端研发指世界水准的尖端研发。今日我们的科技水准，尚未达到世界最尖端，所以应用实施于生产的时机总是晚人一步。如果我们能领先开发尖端技术，并且持续领先，我们的竞争堡垒要比现在强得多。在未来10年，我们要在任何重要技术上领先的机会恐怕不大，所以我们应采取跳蛙策略，看准10年以后的尖端技术何在，现在就开始开发那种技术。尖端研发与基础研究不同。基础研究的目标是增加人类知识，尖端研发则有商业目标。因此，尖端研发应该是企业的责任。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Cutting-edge R&D means R&D at the world's leading edge. Our technological standard today has not yet reached the world's outermost frontier, so we are always a step behind in the timing of applying and implementing technology in production. If we could develop frontier technologies first and keep the lead, our competitive fortress would be far stronger than it is now. Over the next ten years, our chances of leading in any major technology are probably not great, so we should adopt a leapfrog strategy: identify where the frontier technologies of a decade hence will be, and start developing them now. Cutting-edge R&D differs from basic research. The goal of basic research is to increase human knowledge; cutting-edge R&D has commercial objectives. Therefore, cutting-edge R&D should be the responsibility of enterprises.

但尖端研发所需的人才、经费资源极大，即使先进国家的企业界亦需要政府帮助。台湾科技产业与美、日比起来还很小，政府更应助一臂之力。何况政府目前的科技经费已很大，如能善用，对企业界进行尖端开发的帮助可以很大。政府今日的科技经费分配，可以分三大部分。中央研究院从事基础研究，经费应该继续并酌量增加。国科会长久以来投资于小型计划，应加强凝聚资源，开始推动有意义的大项目。其他部会大部分都在做先进国家已做过的东西，很少做尖端研发，更少有计划地锁定10年或15年后的目标，做跳蛙性跃进。

ReadShift 双语翻译

But frontier R&D demands enormous talent and financial resources; even the business communities of advanced countries need government help. Taiwan's technology industry is still very small compared with America's and Japan's, so the government should all the more lend a hand. Moreover, the government's current science and technology budget is already very large; used well, it could greatly help the business community with frontier development. The government's science and technology budget today can be divided into three main parts. The Academia Sinica conducts basic research; its funding should be continued and moderately increased. The National Science Council has long invested in small projects; it should concentrate its resources and begin promoting meaningful large projects. The other ministries and agencies are, for the most part, doing what advanced countries have already done — rarely engaging in frontier R&D, and even more rarely targeting goals ten or fifteen years out in a planned leapfrog.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
public offering—股票上市/公开发行。中文解释：公司股票首次向公众发售，是创业致富的正常途径。
insider trading—内线交易。中文解释：利用未公开信息买卖证券谋利，为各国证券法严格禁止。
timely disclosure—及时公开（财务及营运资料）。中文解释：上市公司向投资人及时披露重要信息的法定义务。
leapfrog strategy—跳蛙策略。中文解释：不逐代追赶，而是直接锁定下一代技术起点、实现跨越式发展。
frontier R&D—尖端研发。中文解释：以商业目标为导向的世界级前沿研究，区别于基础研究。
语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

**设问自答**：以"为什么我称它为……？因为……"建立论述节奏，使抽象的产业判断具象为可追踪的逻辑链。 **对比论证**：尖端研发与基础研究的目标对照（知识 vs. 商业），划清企业责任与政府角色的边界。 **跳蛙策略的理性推演**：承认"未来10年领先机会不大"，转而锁定10年后的目标，是一种务实的战略思维——不恋战于当下，而押注于未来。**Rhetorical question answered in kind**: Framing the argument as "Why do I call it…? Because…" establishes the rhythm of the discussion, turning an abstract industrial judgment into a traceable chain of logic. **Comparative argument**: The contrast between the goals of frontier R&D and basic research (knowledge vs. commerce) draws a clean line between the responsibility of enterprises and the role of government. **The rational logic of the leapfrog strategy**: Admitting that "our chances of leading in the next ten years are slim," then fixing one's sights on where the frontier will be a decade out, is a pragmatic strategic mindset — refusing to be bogged down in the present while betting on the future.

外链知识窗 · Beyond the Text
**美国《商业周刊》（Business Week）**：美国最具影响力的商业杂志之一，1990年代末的报道记录了硅谷科技公司近万家的繁荣图景。 **Business Week**: One of America's most influential business magazines; its reporting in the late 1990s captured the flourishing picture of nearly ten thousand technology companies in Silicon Valley.
**中央研究院**：台湾最高学术研究机构，以基础研究为主；国科会（现科技部）主管科技政策与科研经费分配。 **Academia Sinica**: Taiwan's highest academic research institution, devoted primarily to basic research; the National Science Council (now the Ministry of Science and Technology) oversees science and technology policy and the allocation of research funding.
**硅谷的小公司生态**："野火烧不尽，春风吹又生"——硅谷的高流动率与低创业门槛，使其成为全球创新密度最高的地区。 **Silicon Valley's small-company ecosystem**: "Wildfire cannot burn it out; spring wind makes it grow again" — Silicon Valley's high mobility and low barriers to entrepreneurship make it the region with the highest density of innovation in the world.

我认为政府科技经费中，除了中研院基础研究部分外，只应该做两件事：（一）技术面辅助中小型传统企业，（二）有计划、有规模的尖端突破。平心而论，目前大部分政府研究机构（包括财团法人）的能力都不适合做这两件事。要做，并不是经费问题（现在的经费已经不少），而是人才问题。如果我们能确定政府研发机构的目标，它们就要大量换血。许多现有人才应考虑转入科技产业，同时研究机构要吸收能做尖端研发的精英。

ReadShift 双语翻译

In my view, apart from the Academia Sinica's basic research, government science and technology funds should be spent on only two things: first, technical assistance to small and medium-sized traditional enterprises; and second, planned, large-scale frontier breakthroughs. To be fair, the capabilities of most government research institutions — including corporate foundations — are not suited to either task. Doing them is not a question of money (the current budget is already considerable), but a question of talent. If we can fix the missions of government research institutions, they will need a wholesale transfusion of new blood. Many of the existing researchers should consider moving into the technology industry, while the research institutions must absorb elite scientists capable of frontier R&D.

四、教育改革Education Reform

近十几年来，台湾科技产业有很大的进步，但教育体系却进步很少。也许有人会说，教育改革是需要时间的事。但我们应看看斯坦福和柏克利加州大学。40年前，这两所大学不能和麻省理工学院比，但今日，在许多领域，这两所大学已与麻省理工学院并驾齐驱，且有后来居上之势。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Over the past decade or so, Taiwan's technology industry has made great progress, but its educational system has progressed very little. Some may say educational reform takes time. But consider Stanford and UC Berkeley: forty years ago these two universities could not compare with MIT, yet today, in many fields, they run neck and neck with MIT — and show signs of overtaking it.

这两所大学的进步受硅谷发展之惠，也与硅谷发展有相辅相成的作用。但我们的清大、交大有没有随着新竹科学园区的发展而进步呢？我想答案是：即使有，也不多。我们的教育制度产生了许多精英。台湾科技业之有今日，也大部分拜我们教育制度所产生的人才之赐。但是，如上所述，我们的科技业还只能定位在"技术生产业"上。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Those two universities' progress has benefited from Silicon Valley's development and, in turn, complemented it. But have our Tsing Hua and Chiao Tung universities progressed along with the Hsinchu Science Park? I suspect the answer is: even if somewhat, not much. Our educational system has produced many elites; Taiwan's technology industry owes its present position largely to the talent our educational system has produced. But, as noted above, our technology industry can still only be positioned as a "technology-production industry."

要再进一步，成为一个高障碍的产业，我们必须有许多富于创意、能继续推动科技进步的人才。台湾目前的教育体制，还不能产生足够的这类人才。

ReadShift 双语翻译

To go a step further and become a high-barrier industry, we must have many creative people capable of continuing to advance technology. Taiwan's present educational system cannot yet produce enough of them.

五、内销市场The Domestic Market

美国（尤其硅谷）科技业的发达，一大原因是上下游的密切结合。以半导体业及个人电脑业为例：从事半导体尖端研究与从事电脑尖端研究的人员有频繁接触的机会，他们甚至是好朋友或好邻居。电脑业需要什么新的半导体产品，半导体业的研究人员立刻就知道，而且可随时和需求者切磋讨论；半导体业因本身技术进步而能做出以前未有的新产品，电脑业研究人员也立即知道并可设法应用。

ReadShift 双语翻译

A major reason for the development of America's technology industry — especially Silicon Valley's — is the close integration of upstream and downstream. Take the semiconductor and personal computer industries: researchers at the semiconductor frontier and researchers at the computer frontier have frequent contact; they are even good friends or good neighbors. When the computer industry needs a new semiconductor product, semiconductor researchers know it immediately and can discuss it with the demanders at any time; when the semiconductor industry, through its own technological progress, produces a new product that never existed before, computer researchers likewise learn of it at once and can find ways to apply it.

这样上下游的结合，使得半导体业和个人电脑业都能很快地推进各自的产业尖端科技。

ReadShift 双语翻译

This upstream-downstream integration enables both the semiconductor and the personal computer industries to advance their respective frontier technologies with great speed.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
wholesale transfusion of new blood—大量换血。中文解释：指机构大规模更新人才队伍。
run neck and neck with—与……并驾齐驱。中文解释：双方水平不相上下。
mutually reinforcing—相辅相成。中文解释：双方互相促进、互为支撑。
upstream-downstream integration—上下游结合。中文解释：产业上下游之间紧密协作的机制。
advance the frontier—推进产业尖端。中文解释：把某一领域的技术边界向前推进。
语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

**环环相扣的递进**：人才→教育→市场，三个小节层层推进，从"人才从何而来"到"教育为何滞后"，再到"市场如何塑造创新"，构成完整的因果链。 **对照论证**：斯坦福、柏克利与清大、交大的对照，MIT 与湾区的参照，以美国经验映照台湾问题，客观而有说服力。 **以产业逻辑论教育**：不空谈教育理念，而从"高障碍产业需要什么样的人才"反推教育改革的必要，是艾萨克森式的"从结果倒推原因"的叙事方法。**Interlocking progression**: Talent → education → market — three subsections advancing layer by layer, from "where does talent come from" to "why has education lagged behind" and then to "how the market shapes innovation," building a complete causal chain. **Comparative argument**: Stanford and Berkeley set against Tsing Hua and Chiao Tung, with MIT and the Bay Area as reference points — holding up American experience as a mirror to Taiwan's problems in an objective and persuasive way. **Discussing education through industrial logic**: Rather than preaching abstract educational ideals, the author reasons back from "what kind of talent a high-barrier industry needs" to the necessity of educational reform — an Isaacson-style narrative of "reasoning from the result back to the cause."

外链知识窗 · Beyond the Text
**斯坦福与柏克利**：湾区双雄与硅谷共生共荣——斯坦福的产学研传统与柏克利的工程教育，是硅谷人才与技术的两大源头。 **Stanford and Berkeley**: The Bay Area's twin titans thrived symbiotically with Silicon Valley — Stanford's industry-academia tradition and Berkeley's engineering education form the two great fountains of Silicon Valley talent and technology.
**清大、交大与新竹科学园区**：台湾清华大学与交通大学毗邻新竹科学园区，本应复刻"大学—园区"共生模式，但作者认为其进步有限，是台湾教育体制的缩影。 **Tsing Hua, Chiao Tung, and the Hsinchu Science Park**: Taiwan's Tsing Hua University and National Chiao Tung University sit adjacent to the Hsinchu Science Park and should have replicated the "university–park" symbiosis, yet the author sees their progress as limited — a microcosm of Taiwan's educational system.
**麻省理工学院（MIT）**：美国工程教育的标杆，40年前斯坦福与柏克利无法企及，如今在诸多领域已并驾齐驱——说明教育是可以被追赶的。 **Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)**: The benchmark of American engineering education; forty years ago Stanford and Berkeley could not match it, yet today they run neck and neck in many fields — proof that education can be caught up with.

台湾科技业缺乏广大的内销市场，所以我们的下游都在国外。台湾个人电脑业如要了解市场的需要，就须去国外，再把这需要告诉岛内半导体业，当然迟了一步。相反，台湾半导体业如有能力做出尖端产品，是去找与市场有密切接触的国外电脑公司呢？还是去找与市场有隔阂的台湾电脑业？结论当然是找国外电脑业。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Taiwan's technology industry lacks a large domestic market, so our downstream customers are all overseas. If Taiwan's PC industry wants to understand market needs, it must go abroad and then convey those needs to the island's semiconductor industry — a step late, to be sure. Conversely, if Taiwan's semiconductor industry can make frontier products, does it go to foreign computer companies in close contact with the market, or to Taiwan's computer industry, which is cut off from the market? The conclusion is naturally to go to the foreign computer companies.

没有广大腹地市场，也因此失去上下游的密切结合的机制，是科技业持续发展的大障碍。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Without a large domestic market, and thereby losing the mechanism of close upstream-downstream integration, a major obstacle stands in the way of the technology industry's sustained development.

六、生活品质Quality of Life

台湾科技业人员的收入，在十几年前远不及美国。今日大部分已达到美国相等人员水准，少数甚且超出美国水准。随着收入的提高，大家对生活的要求也有改变。十几年前，新竹园区绿树成荫的工作环境被认为非常优美，为难得之作，今天大部分人已只把它当作标准。十几年前，新竹园区的员工宿舍被认为豪华，现在大部分人却觉得不够水准。污染、噪音、塞车等等现象，十几年前或不严重，或不受注意，但是今天造成严重不满，区内、区外人人怨声载道。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The incomes of Taiwan's technology workers, far below their American counterparts a decade or so ago, have today mostly reached the level of their American peers, and a few even exceed it. With rising incomes, people's demands on life have also changed. A dozen years ago, the tree-shaded working environment of the Hsinchu Science Park was considered very beautiful, a rare achievement; today most people treat it as merely standard. A dozen years ago, the employee dormitories of the Hsinchu park were considered luxurious; now most people find them substandard. Pollution, noise, traffic jams — a dozen years ago these were either not serious or not noticed, but today they cause grave discontent, and complaints are heard from everyone inside and outside the park.

除了属物质层面的生活品质外，还有文化方面的生活品质。例如治安、社会公义、廉洁政府、扫除黑金势力威胁等等。也许以前这些问题没有现在严重，也许以前较被容忍，但现在不但不满此种现象的心态更形扩张，而且普遍认为是严重侵蚀整体竞争力的毒素。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Besides the material dimension of quality of life, there is the cultural dimension: public order, social justice, an honest government, the removal of the threat of organized money politics, and so on. Perhaps these problems were not as serious before, or perhaps they were more tolerated; but now not only has discontent with such phenomena spread, they are widely regarded as a poison that seriously erodes the nation's overall competitiveness.

美国现在仍是吸引全世界人才的磁石。许多事业有成的华裔人才在彼扎根，也有赴美求学的台湾青年学成不归。为什么美国仍是这样的磁石？现在已不能仅仅怪待遇的差异了。主要原因是美国物质上和文化上的生活品质。

ReadShift 双语翻译

America remains a magnet attracting talent from all over the world. Many successful ethnic Chinese professionals have put down roots there, and Taiwanese young people who studied in America often do not return after completing their studies. Why is America still such a magnet? No longer can pay differentials alone be blamed. The main reason is America's material and cultural quality of life.

七、内在变革Inner Transformation

台湾文化本有许多优点，使科技业能有今日的成就：重视教育、勤奋、敬业。但近年来，这些美德似乎在消退，取而代之的是贪婪、短视、投机、走捷径等积习，而且产生劣币驱逐良币的作用。若不扭转，台湾社会将变成正派的人不愿出头、不肯前进的社会，这与高科技的持续发展完全不相容。我们需要大量有使命感、有创新能力的精英在台湾安居乐业。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Taiwanese culture possesses many strengths that have propelled its tech industry to its present achievement: a deep reverence for education, industry, and professional dedication. Yet in recent years these virtues seem to be fading. In their place, corrosive habits have taken root — greed, short-sightedness, speculation, the pursuit of shortcuts. Worse, they carry the force of Gresham's Law, driving out the better sort. Unless reversed, Taiwanese society risks becoming one where decent people hold back and refuse to advance — a condition wholly incompatible with sustained high-tech development. What is needed is a large number of people with a sense of mission and creative ability, settled and thriving in Taiwan.

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
a magnet drawing talent—吸引人才的磁石。中文解释：比喻对人才有强大吸引力的地方。
Gresham's Law—格雷欣法则（劣币驱逐良币）。中文解释：经济学定律，此处比喻坏风气排挤好风气。
poison corroding competitiveness—侵蚀竞争力的毒素。中文解释：比喻严重损害整体竞争力的因素。
settle and thrive (安居乐业)—安居乐业。中文解释：安于居所、乐于本业，指人才愿意长期扎根发展。
语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

**由物质到文化的递进**：生活品质一节从收入、环境等物质层面，递进到治安、公义、廉洁等文化层面，再上升到"内在变革"的精神层面，层层深入。 **磁石之问**："为什么美国仍是这样的磁石？"设问之后，否定了简单的待遇解释，把答案指向文化与制度的综合品质——艾萨克森式的追问方法。 **格雷欣法则的隐喻**：以"劣币驱逐良币"比喻坏风气排挤好风气的社会病理，为"改革是最难的一步"埋下伏笔。**A progression from the material to the cultural**: The quality-of-life section ascends from material concerns such as income and environment, to cultural ones such as public order, justice, and clean government, and finally to the spiritual dimension of "inner transformation" — going ever deeper layer by layer. **The magnet question**: "Why is America still such a magnet?" After posing the question, the author dismisses the simple pay-differential explanation and points the answer toward the composite quality of culture and institutions — an Isaacson-style method of inquiry. **The metaphor of Gresham's Law**: Using "bad money drives out good" as an analogy for the social pathology in which bad practices crowd out good ones, foreshadowing the claim that "reform is the hardest step."

外链知识窗 · Beyond the Text
**新竹科学园区**：1980年设立，台湾第一个科学园区，被誉为"台湾硅谷"，是台湾科技业起飞的核心载体。 **Hsinchu Science Park**: Established in 1980 as Taiwan's first science park, it has been hailed as "Taiwan's Silicon Valley" and served as the core vehicle for the takeoff of Taiwan's technology industry.
**黑金政治**：1990年代台湾舆论对金钱与政治势力勾结现象的统称，是当时社会批评的焦点之一。 **Black-gold politics**: A term used by Taiwan's public discourse in the 1990s for the collusion between money and political power — one of the focal points of social criticism at the time.
**《发展台湾科技业》的写作背景**：1997年9月应"行政院长"萧万长之邀而作，正值亚洲金融风暴爆发，文中对投资环境与人才流失的忧虑带有鲜明的时代印记。 **The background of "Developing Taiwan's Technology Sector"**: Written in September 1997 at the invitation of Premier Vincent Siew, in the midst of the Asian financial crisis; the essay's anxieties over the investment environment and brain drain bear a distinctive stamp of its era.

政府应正视病根所在，努力、尽快提供一个能够吸引、留住这种人才的环境。

ReadShift 双语翻译

The government must face squarely where the root of the disease lies, and work hard and quickly to provide an environment that can attract and retain such talent.

结语Conclusion

对台湾而言，科技产业将是迈入发达世界的最后一步，恐怕也是最难的一步。科技产业最重要的是人才，我们如何培养、吸引、保留这些人才，让他们在此安居乐业，尽量发挥？改善这些关于人才的条件，也就是强化整体经济的基本环境。局部措施如科学园区、租税优惠、研发增强等等，可以建立低竞争障碍的技术生产业，但不能建立高障碍的尖端科技业。近来"科技岛"成为一个响亮的口号，但如果没有基本的改革，科技岛是做不成的。

ReadShift 双语翻译

For Taiwan, the technology industry will be the final step into the developed world — and probably the hardest. The most important thing in the technology industry is talent. How do we cultivate, attract, and retain these people, and let them settle, thrive, and realize their full potential here? Improving these conditions for talent is, in effect, strengthening the basic environment of the whole economy. Piecemeal measures such as science parks, tax incentives, and enhanced R&D can build a low-barrier technology-production industry, but cannot build a high-barrier frontier technology industry. Lately "Technology Island" has become a resounding slogan — but without fundamental reform, a Technology Island cannot be built.

在我们的科技产业还没有达到足以遍及全岛的规模之前，来自别的国家、地区的激烈竞争已将使我们成长转缓！台湾具有成为科技岛的基本体制：民主和自由经济。民族文化也具备塑造科技岛出现的条件。但在现在体制及传统文化下，还需要许多改革、进步。这些改革尽管是最难的一步，却是台湾能否在21世纪成为发达社会的必要之途。（此文系于1997年9月，未曾对外公开发表。）

ReadShift 双语翻译

Before our technology industry has reached a scale sufficient to spread across the whole island, fierce competition from other countries and regions will already have slowed our growth! Taiwan possesses the basic institutions to become a Technology Island: democracy and a free-market economy. Its national culture, too, contains the conditions for a Technology Island to emerge. But under the present institutions and traditional culture, much reform and progress are still needed. Difficult as these reforms are — the hardest step — they are the necessary road for Taiwan to become a developed society in the twenty-first century. (This essay was written in September 1997 and had never been published.)

Cheat Sheet · 商业语汇
take root and flourish—扎根并繁茂。中文解释：字面意为"扎根并繁茂"，商业语境中常用来形容人才、企业或项目在特定环境中稳定落脚后持续成长、释放价值。
human capital—人力资本。中文解释：经济学标准术语，指通过教育、培训与健康投资所积累的人的知识、技能与创造力，被视为驱动产业升级与长期经济增长的核心资产。
piecemeal initiatives—零散措施。中文解释：指缺乏系统规划、仅针对局部问题做出的分散性政策或行动，隐含"治标不治本"之意，常与"comprehensive/foundational reform"对举使用。
sap growth momentum—侵蚀发展势头。中文解释：形象化商业表达，指外部压力或内部结构性问题逐渐侵蚀、消耗原本强劲的发展势头，多用于宏观经济、市场趋势或企业业绩分析。
语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

**收束全篇的结语**：把"人才—教育—市场—生活品质—文化"诸节归结为一点——人才是科技产业的根本，改善人才条件就是强化整体经济的基本环境。 **口号与现实的对照**："科技岛"口号响亮，但没有基本改革就做不成——以最克制的语气说出最严厉的判断，是艾萨克森式的笔法。 **未竟之章**：文末注明"未曾对外公开发表"，与开篇"应萧万长之邀而写"呼应，一篇内部建言的分量尽在其中。**A conclusion that gathers the whole essay**: It folds the sections on talent, education, market, quality of life, and culture into a single point — talent is the root of the technology industry, and improving the conditions for talent is tantamount to strengthening the basic environment of the entire economy. **The contrast between slogan and reality**: The "Technology Island" slogan is resounding, but without fundamental reform it cannot be realized — stating the harshest judgment in the most restrained tone, a distinctly Isaacson-like touch. **An unfinished chapter**: The closing note that the essay "had never been published" echoes the opening reference to its having been written at Premier Vincent Siew's invitation, and in that echo lies the full weight of an internal policy brief.

外链知识窗 · Beyond the Text
**1997年亚洲金融风暴**：1997年7月从泰国爆发并席卷亚洲，台湾因经济基本面较稳受影响较小，但《发展台湾科技业》成文于此背景之下，对投资环境的忧虑有其现实根源。 **The 1997 Asian financial crisis**: It broke out in Thailand in July 1997 and swept across Asia; Taiwan was less affected thanks to its relatively sound economic fundamentals, yet "Developing Taiwan's Technology Sector" was written against this backdrop, and its concerns about the investment environment have a real-world root.
**"科技岛"愿景**：1990年代台湾提出的科技立岛政策口号，其后以竹科、南科等科学园区为载体逐步落地，台积电等企业的发展使其部分成为现实。 **The "Technology Island" vision**: A policy slogan proposed in Taiwan in the 1990s for building the island on technology; it was gradually realized through vehicles such as the Hsinchu and Tainan science parks, and partly came true through the rise of companies such as TSMC.

张忠谋大事年表A Chronology of Morris Chang (1931–1998)

1931年◎出生于浙江宁波。1932年◎随父母迁南京。1936年◎在南京入小学。1937年◎随父母迁广州。◎抗日战争开始，广州遭日机轰炸，随父母迁香港。1941年◎珍珠港事变发生。日军占领香港。1942年自小学毕业。1943年◎随父母长途跋涉至重庆。◎入重庆沙坪坝南开中学。1945年◎抗战胜利。

ReadShift 双语翻译

1931 — Born in Ningbo, Zhejiang. 1932 — Moved with his parents to Nanjing. 1936 — Entered primary school in Nanjing. 1937 — Moved with his parents to Guangzhou; with the outbreak of the War of Resistance and the Japanese bombing of Guangzhou, the family moved to Hong Kong. 1941 — The attack on Pearl Harbor; Japanese forces occupied Hong Kong. 1942 — Graduated from primary school. 1943 — Made the long journey with his parents to Chongqing; entered Nankai Middle School in Shapingba, Chongqing. 1945 — Victory in the War of Resistance.

随父母迁上海。1948年◎毕业于上海南洋模范中学。同年底随父母迁香港。◎夏克雷、布律登及巴丁在美国贝尔实验室发明晶体管。1949年◎赴美国哈佛大学入大学一年级。1950年◎转学麻省理工学院二年级。1952年◎获麻省理工学院机械系学士学位。◎美国贝尔实验室授权厂商生产晶体管。半导体业在美国诞生。1953年◎获麻省理工学院机械系硕士学位。1955年◎进入半导体业，就职希凡尼亚公司半导体部。1958年◎入德州仪器公司。

ReadShift 双语翻译

Moved with his parents to Shanghai. 1948 — Graduated from Nanyang Model High School in Shanghai; at year's end moved with his parents to Hong Kong. Shockley, Bardeen, and Brattain invented the transistor at Bell Laboratories in America. 1949 — Entered Harvard University as a freshman. 1950 — Transferred to MIT as a sophomore. 1952 — Received a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from MIT. Bell Laboratories licensed manufacturers to produce transistors; the semiconductor industry was born in America. 1953 — Received a master's degree in mechanical engineering from MIT. 1955 — Entered the semiconductor industry, joining the semiconductor division of Sylvania. 1958 — Joined Texas Instruments.

Shaping global industrial landscape—重塑全球工业格局。
Threshold of a new era—新时代的门槛。
语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

**编年体的克制**：年表以年份为骨架，只录事实，不作评价——战争、迁徙、求学、入行，全部压缩在最短的句子里，让读者自己体味其中的颠沛与坚韧。 **个人与时代的双线**：1948年晶体管发明与1949年赴美求学并置，暗示个人命运与半导体革命即将交汇；1958年入德仪，正是产业爆发前夜。 **数字的留白**：1931到1958，二十七年间的迁徙轨迹（宁波→南京→广州→香港→重庆→上海→香港→美国）无需渲染，已然惊心动魄。**The restraint of the chronicle**: With the years as its skeleton, the chronology records only facts and passes no judgment — war, displacement, schooling, and entry into the industry are all compressed into the shortest sentences, letting readers savor the turbulence and tenacity for themselves. **The twin tracks of an individual and an era**: Placing the invention of the transistor in 1948 beside his departure for America to study in 1949 hints that a personal destiny and the semiconductor revolution were about to converge; his joining Texas Instruments in 1958 came precisely on the eve of the industry's explosion. **The eloquence of dates**: From 1931 to 1958, the migratory arc of twenty-seven years — Ningbo → Nanjing → Guangzhou → Hong Kong → Chongqing → Shanghai → Hong Kong → America — needs no embellishment; it is already breathtaking.

**肖克利、巴丁、布拉顿**：1947年在贝尔实验室发明点接触式晶体管，1956年获诺贝尔物理学奖。 **Shockley, Bardeen, and Brattain**: Invented the point-contact transistor at Bell Laboratories in 1947 and won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1956.
**希凡尼亚公司（Sylvania）**：美国老牌电子企业，其半导体部门曾是半导体产业早期的重要参与者。 **Sylvania**: A long-established American electronics company whose semiconductor division was once an important player in the early days of the semiconductor industry.
**德州仪器（TI）**：张忠谋在此经历了半导体产业的黄金时代，后于1987年创立台积电，被誉为"芯片大王"。 **Texas Instruments (TI)**: The company where Morris Chang experienced the golden age of the semiconductor industry; he later founded TSMC in 1987 and came to be hailed as the "chip king."
**沙坪坝南开中学**：1936年由张伯苓在重庆沙坪坝创办，抗战时期培养了大量杰出人才。 **Nankai Middle School, Shapingba**: Founded by Chang Po-ling in Shapingba, Chongqing in 1936, it trained a great many outstanding talents during the War of Resistance.

1982 — Sun Yun-suan and Li Kuo-ting invited him to return to serve in Taiwan; the invitation came to nothing. 1983 — Resigned from Texas Instruments. 1984 — President of General Instrument Corporation. 1985 — Resigned as president of General Instrument; at the invitation of Yu Kuo-hwa, Li Kuo-ting, and Hsu Hsiu-shu (chairman of the Industrial Technology Research Institute), went to Taiwan to serve as president of ITRI. 1986 — Founded Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) and served as its chairman. 1988 — Resigned as ITRI president, remaining chairman of TSMC. 1989 — The Hsin Chong Enterprise Group and other investors jointly acquired American Wyse Technology; he was invited to serve as its chairman. 1997 — Resigned as ITRI chairman; TSMC listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange; founded Vanguard International Semiconductor Corporation and served as its chairman.

语言与逻辑赏析 · Language & Logic Appreciation

本段传记采用**时间线性叙事**配合**因果递进**结构，以张忠谋的职业生涯为轴，串联起台湾半导体产业从无到有的历史脉络。艾萨克森风格的精髓在于：**不直接评价，而通过细节与选择呈现人物的战略眼光**。例如，1982年婉拒回台与1985年接受邀请形成对照，揭示当时台湾基础设施尚未成熟的现实判断；而"创办台积电"这一决定改变了全球半导体产业的地图，传记以事实的排列代替颂扬，体现传记文学的克制笔法。This biographical passage employs **linear chronological narration** combined with a **cause-and-effect progression** structure, using Morris Chang's career as its axis to string together the arc of Taiwan's semiconductor industry from nothing to something. The essence of the Isaacson style lies in **not judging directly, but revealing a figure's strategic vision through details and choices**. For instance, the contrast between declining to return to Taiwan in 1982 and accepting the invitation in 1985 discloses a realistic assessment that Taiwan's infrastructure was not yet mature; and the decision to "found TSMC" redrew the map of the global semiconductor industry. The biography substitutes the arrangement of facts for eulogy, embodying the restraint characteristic of biographical literature.

背景知识延伸 · Beyond the Text
**台积电的开创性模式**：张忠谋首创的"纯代工"（pure-play foundry）模式打破了垂直整合的行业惯例——台积电不生产自有品牌芯片，而是为其他设计公司代工制造。这一模式降低了半导体创业的门槛，催生了高通、英伟达、苹果等无厂芯片设计公司的崛起，间接塑造了今日全球科技产业的分工格局。 **TSMC's pioneering model**: The "pure-play foundry" model that Morris Chang pioneered broke with the industry convention of vertical integration — TSMC produces no chips under its own brand but manufactures on behalf of other design companies. This model lowered the barriers to semiconductor entrepreneurship, gave rise to fabless chip-design firms such as Qualcomm, NVIDIA, and Apple, and indirectly shaped today's global division of labor in the technology industry.
**孙运璇与李国鼎**：两人是台湾战后经济奇迹的关键推手。孙运璇主导十大建设，李国鼎推动科技产业政策，他们的愿景为台积电的诞生提供了制度与人才土壤。 **Sun Yun-suan and Li Kuo-ting**: The two men were key drivers of Taiwan's postwar economic miracle. Sun Yun-suan led the Ten Major Construction Projects, while Li Kuo-ting advanced technology-industry policy; their vision provided the institutional and human-resource soil from which TSMC was born.

外链知识窗

**通用器材公司（General Instrument）**：美国老牌电子企业，张忠谋1984年任其总裁，1985年辞任。 **General Instrument**: A long-established American electronics company; Morris Chang served as its president from 1984 and resigned in 1985.
**慧智科技（Wyse Technology）**：美国终端设备厂商，1989年被和信企业集团等并购，张忠谋出任董事长，是其将台湾资本与美国技术连结的首次尝试。 **Wyse Technology**: An American terminal-equipment maker acquired in 1989 by the Hsin Chong Enterprise Group and others, with Morris Chang serving as chairman — his first attempt to link Taiwanese capital with American technology.
**世界先进集成电路公司（Vanguard International Semiconductor）**：台湾晶圆代工企业，源自台积电体系，张忠谋任董事长。 **Vanguard International Semiconductor**: A Taiwanese wafer foundry that grew out of the TSMC system; Morris Chang served as its chairman.

**纽交所上市（NYSE Debut）的倍增效应**：1997年登陆纽交所不仅是融资行为，更是一次品牌信用背书，使这家台湾企业首次以"全球公司"身份进入国际投资者视野。 **The multiplier effect of the NYSE debut**: Listing on the New York Stock Exchange in 1997 was not merely a fundraising act but also an endorsement of brand credibility, bringing this Taiwanese company into the view of international investors for the first time as a "global company."

**茅盾文学奖**：由中国作家茅盾捐资设立，1982年首次颁发，是中国最具权威的长篇小说奖项，获奖者包括路遥《平凡的世界》、陈忠实《白鹿原》、莫言《生死疲劳》等。 **Mao Dun Literature Prize**: Endowed by the Chinese writer Mao Dun and first awarded in 1982, it is China's most authoritative award for long-form fiction; winners include Lu Yao's *The Ordinary World*, Chen Zhongshi's *White Deer Plain*, and Mo Yan's *Life and Death Are Wearing Me Out*.
**豆瓣读书**：成立于2005年，是中国最大的中文图书社区，其年度榜单反映的是"文艺青年"和深度阅读群体的审美取向，与纯商业畅销书榜单形成有趣对照。 **Douban Reading**: Founded in 2005, it is China's largest Chinese-language book community; its annual charts reflect the aesthetic preferences of "literary youth" and deeply engaged reading circles, forming an interesting contrast with purely commercial best-seller charts.
**"给五星都不够"文化**：源于亚马逊的五星评价体系的隐喻——当用户认为某物卓越到现有评分系统无法承载时，便产生此类表达，常见于Goodreads和高评分社群。 **The "five stars aren't enough" culture**: A metaphor rooted in Amazon's five-star rating system — when users find something so outstanding that the existing rating scale cannot contain it, such expressions arise; they are commonly seen on Goodreads and in high-rated communities.

Past winners include Lu Yao's *The Ordinary World*, Chen Zhongshi's *White Deer Plain*, Mo Yan's *Life and Death Are Wearing Me Out*, and Chi Zijian's *The Last Quarter of the Moon*, representing the highest standard of contemporary Chinese literary creation.
**豆瓣读书年度榜单**：成立于2005年，是中国最大的中文图书社区。其年度榜单反映的是"文艺青年"和深度阅读群体的审美取向，与纯商业畅销书榜单形成有趣的对照——豆瓣高分书未必是最畅销的，但往往具有更持久的文化价值。 **Douban Reading annual charts**: Founded in 2005, it is China's largest Chinese-language book community. Its annual charts reflect the aesthetic preferences of "literary youth" and deeply engaged reading circles, forming an interesting contrast with purely commercial best-seller charts — Douban's high-scored books are not necessarily the best sellers, but they often carry more enduring cultural value.
**"给五星都不够"文化**：源于亚马逊等平台的五星评价体系的隐喻表达。当用户认为某作品的卓越程度已超出既有评分系统的承载能力时，便产生此类表达。这种现象在 Goodreads 和高评分社群中尤为常见，体现了一种**评分系统的溢出效应**。 **The "five stars aren't enough" culture**: A metaphorical expression rooted in the five-star rating systems of platforms such as Amazon. When users judge a work's excellence to exceed the capacity of the existing rating scale, such expressions arise. The phenomenon is especially common on Goodreads and in high-rated communities, embodying a **spillover effect of the rating system**.
**亚马逊编辑推荐 vs 算法推荐**：亚马逊的编辑推荐书单强调"人"的判断力——由资深读者和图书销售人员基于长期观察形成，而非完全依赖用户购买数据的算法排序。这种 "curated vs algorithmic" 的张力，是当前内容平台普遍面临的经典命题。 **Amazon's editorial picks vs. algorithmic recommendations**: Amazon's editor-recommended reading lists emphasize human judgment — formed by seasoned readers and booksellers based on long-term observation, rather than relying entirely on algorithmic ranking of user purchase data. This "curated vs. algorithmic" tension is a classic proposition that content platforms today universally face.
